values.doc: Fixed at `offset`, read as a world position.

values.name: STURDY_AUDIO_ATTACH_ENTITY

enums.doc:
Graphics backend to request.

enums.name: SturdyBackendMask
enums.doc: Bitmask of graphics backends (see `SturdyBackend`) a physical GPU can be used with, as reported by `sturdy_gpu_enumerate`.

enums.name: SturdyBindingType
enums.doc: What a bind-group-layout entry binds.

enums.doc: Swapchain color space, including real display HDR transfer functions. Matches `RHI::ColorSpace`. `STURDY_COLOR_SPACE_DOLBY_VISION` is declared for completeness but not implemented by either backend yet; requesting it will not succeed.

enums.name: SturdyCursorIcon
enums.doc: Cursor shapes a window can request.

enums.name: SturdyDeviceType
enums.doc: Broad class of a physical device — the engine's active one (`SturdyAdapterInfo::device_type`) or one reported by `sturdy_gpu_enumerate` before any engine exists.

enums.name: SturdyFieldKind
enums.doc: The scalar kinds a component field can have (since 0.35). These are what two languages must agree on to share a component's memory: a C `float`, a Rust `f32` and a C# `float` are all `STURDY_FIELD_F32`. Values never change.

enums.name: SturdyFormat
enums.doc:
Pixel format for a texture, or a vertex/color-target format reference.

Ordinal values are pinned to match the engine's internal `RHI::Format` and must stay in this exact order; new formats are appended, never inserted.

enums.name: SturdyFrameRateLimitMode
enums.doc: The "FPS Limit" dial: how the render loop caps its own dispatch rate, independent of and composing with whatever the resolved present mode is already doing. Matches `Core::FrameRateLimitMode`.

values.name: STURDY_FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_MODE_UNLIMITED
values.doc: No engine-imposed cap. Correct with a vsync-blocking present mode (Fifo/FifoLatestReady); with a non-blocking one (Mailbox/Immediate/FifoRelaxed) this really is uncapped dispatch, an explicit choice rather than something the engine silently overrides.

values.name: STURDY_FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_MODE_CUSTOM
values.doc: Cap dispatch to `SturdyPresentationSettings::frame_rate_limit_fps`, regardless of present mode.

values.name: STURDY_FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_MODE_MATCH_DISPLAY_REFRESH
values.doc: Cap dispatch to the display's current refresh rate (queried per frame; a window can move between displays with different rates). Falls back to unlimited if the platform/window can't report one.

enums.name: SturdyFrontFace
enums.doc: Winding considered front-facing by the rasterizer.

enums.name: SturdyGltfLightKind
enums.doc: What kind of light a glTF file declared.

enums.name: SturdyHdrColorGamut
enums.doc: A display's reported color gamut. Matches `RHI::HdrColorGamut`.

enums.name: SturdyHdrColorSpaceMode
enums.doc: Real display HDR transfer function/color-space combination to present in, when `SturdyPresentationSettings::hdr_enabled` is set. Matches `Core::HdrColorSpaceMode`.

enums.name: SturdyHdrMetadataConfidence
enums.doc: How much to trust reported HDR display metadata. Matches `RHI::HdrMetadataConfidence`.

enums.name: SturdyHdrMetadataSource
enums.doc: Where reported HDR display metadata came from. Matches `RHI::HdrMetadataSource`.

enums.name: SturdyHdrTransferFunction
enums.doc: A display's reported HDR transfer function. Matches `RHI::HdrTransferFunction`.

enums.name: SturdyLatencyMode
enums.doc: Presentation latency policy. Matches `Core::LatencyMode`.

enums.name: SturdyLoadOp
enums.doc: Load/store behavior for a render pass attachment.

enums.name: SturdyLogLevel
enums.doc: Severity of a log message.

enums.name: SturdyMemoryLocation
enums.doc: Where a buffer's backing memory lives.

enums.name: SturdyMouseButton
enums.doc: Mouse buttons, matching the engine's own ordering.

enums.name: SturdyOpacityMicromapFormat
enums.doc: Matches `RHI::OpacityMicromapFormat`.

enums.name: SturdyPlatformQueryStatus
enums.doc: Outcome of a platform-level display/HDR query, distinct from `SturdyResult`: the call itself succeeded (a device and surface exist), but the platform may still have nothing useful to report. Matches `RHI::PlatformQueryStatus`.

enums.name: SturdyPluginLoadFlags
enums.doc: Flags for `SturdyPluginLoadDesc::flags`.

values.name: STURDY_PLUGIN_SHADOW_COPY
values.doc: Copy the library to a unique temporary file and open the copy, so the original can be rebuilt while the plugin runs.

values.name: STURDY_PLUGIN_LOAD_FLAGS_FORCE_32
values.doc: Copy the library to a unique temporary file and open the copy, so the original can be rebuilt while the plugin runs.

enums.name: SturdyPluginReason
enums.doc: Why the engine is calling a plugin's entry point.

values.name: STURDY_PLUGIN_LOAD
values.doc: The library was just opened. Describe the plugin and add its modules through the host table.

values.name: STURDY_PLUGIN_UNLOAD
values.doc: Every module has been destroyed and the library is about to be closed. Release whatever `set_state` stored.

values.name: STURDY_PLUGIN_REASON_FORCE_32
values.doc: Every module has been destroyed and the library is about to be closed. Release whatever `set_state` stored.

values.name: STURDY_POLYGON_MODE_LINE
values.doc: Wireframe. A device feature on some backends; check before relying on it.

values.name: STURDY_POLYGON_MODE_POINT
values.doc: Wireframe. A device feature on some backends; check before relying on it.

enums.name: SturdyPresentMode
enums.doc: Concrete swapchain present mode a `SturdyPresentStrategy` resolved to on this backend. Matches `RHI::PresentMode`.

enums.name: SturdyPresentStrategy
enums.doc: How the engine should schedule presentation relative to the display's refresh cycle, once vsync/VRR/latency are taken into account. Matches `RHI::PresentStrategy`.

enums.name: SturdyPresentationPreference
enums.doc: Overall presentation tuning goal. Matches `Core::PresentationPreference`.

enums.name: SturdyQueryType
enums.doc: Kind of work a query set records.

enums.name: SturdyQueueCapability
enums.doc: Bit flags describing what a queue can do. Combined with bitwise OR in `SturdyQueueInfo::capabilities`.

enums.name: SturdyQueueClass
enums.doc: Class of work a queue accepts.

enums.name: SturdyRayTracingShaderGroupType
enums.doc: Matches `RHI::RayTracingShaderGroupType`.

enums.name: SturdyRenderFeature
enums.doc: Render-graph stages that can be toggled per frame.

values.name: STURDY_RENDER_FEATURE_FRAME_TIMINGS
values.doc: Collect frame timings for `Renderer::last_frame_timings` (an application's own diagnostics overlay reads them).

values.name: STURDY_RENDER_FEATURE_DEBUG_OVERLAY

values.doc: Deprecated alias: the engine no longer draws a debug overlay; this now only enables frame timings.

values.doc: Deprecated alias: the engine no longer draws a debug overlay; this now only enables frame timings.

enums.name: SturdyRestirGiDenoiser
enums.doc: Denoiser resolving ReSTIR GI's raw reservoir output. `DLSS_RAY_RECONSTRUCTION`/`FSR_REDSTONE` are reserved for future vendor-SDK integrations; selecting either falls back to `SVGF` with a one-time engine warning until a real backend exists.

enums.name: SturdyResult
enums.doc:
Status returned by every fallible entry point.

Each enum in this header carries an explicit `0x7fffffff` sentinel so the underlying type is a full 32 bits on every compiler, rather than something a compiler may narrow to `char` or `short` based on the values present.

values.name: STURDY_OK
values.doc: The call succeeded.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
values.doc: A required pointer was null, or a value was outside its documented range.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE
values.doc: A handle was never valid, or carried the wrong kind.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_HANDLE_EXPIRED
values.doc: A handle was valid once but its callback scope has ended. See the handle scope rules above.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_STRUCT_SIZE
values.doc: A `struct_size` field did not match any layout this engine build understands.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED
values.doc: The engine failed to initialize; the window or graphics device could not be created.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_CALLBACK_FAILED
values.doc: A caller-supplied callback reported failure.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_ALREADY_RUNNING
values.doc: A runtime is already executing in this process. Only one may run at a time.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
values.doc: An allocation failed.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_INTERNAL
values.doc: An unexpected internal failure. `sturdy_last_error_message()` carries the detail.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL
values.doc: A supplied text buffer was too small. The output length was still written; call again with a buffer of that size.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE
values.doc: The requested capability is not present on this device or in this build — a Vulkan handle query on a D3D12 device, or a native handle query when native access was not enabled.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE
values.doc: An index was past the end of the collection being enumerated.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_ENTITY_NOT_ALIVE
values.doc: The entity was never valid, or has been destroyed. Expected in ordinary use — an entity can die between the frame you stored it and the frame you used it.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_MISSING
values.doc: The entity does not carry the requested component.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_PRESENT
values.doc: The entity already carries that component.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_NOT_BLITTABLE
values.doc: The component cannot be accessed as raw bytes because its C++ type is not trivially copyable. See `sturdy_ecs_component_info`.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_BUSY
values.doc: The world cannot be changed right now — an iteration is in progress on this thread, or a system schedule is running.

values.name: STURDY_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST
values.doc: The GPU device was lost (driver crash/reset, surprise-removed adapter, ...). Every resource and command buffer from before this point is invalid; the engine cannot recover within this process.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_CUBE

values.doc: Uses `extents_x`, `extents_y`, `extents_z`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_ICO_SPHERE
values.doc: Uses `radius`, `subdivisions`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_PLANE
values.doc: Uses `width`, `depth`, `width_segments`, `depth_segments`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_CYLINDER
values.doc: Uses `radius`, `height`, `radial_segments`, `capped`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_CONE
values.doc: Uses `radius`, `height`, `radial_segments`, `capped`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_TORUS
values.doc: Uses `major_radius`, `minor_radius`, `major_segments`, `minor_segments`.

values.name: STURDY_SHAPE_TETRAHEDRON
values.doc: Uses `size`.

enums.name: SturdyTaskWeight
enums.doc: How much work a task represents, which decides where the scheduler puts it.

values.name: STURDY_TASK_LIGHT
values.doc: Short work. Queued where latency matters more than throughput.

values.name: STURDY_TASK_HEAVY
values.doc: Long work. Kept off the lanes that short tasks depend on, so one heavy job cannot stall a frame's worth of small ones.

enums.name: SturdyTextureDimension
enums.doc: Dimensionality of a texture.

enums.name: SturdyTextureLayout
enums.doc: Layout a texture is transitioned to/from by a barrier.

enums.name: SturdyTextureViewType
enums.doc: How a texture view's subresources are addressed.

enums.name: SturdyToneMapping
enums.doc: Tone-mapping operator applied to the scene's HDR output.

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_DETAIL_OFF
values.doc: Nothing is captured.

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_DETAIL_SCOPES
values.doc: Foreign call site and engine scopes only. Cheap enough to leave on in release builds. The release-build default.

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_DETAIL_NATIVE
values.doc: Scopes plus the native call stack. The debug-build default.

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_FRAME_NATIVE
values.doc: A machine frame: `address`, `module`, `module_offset`, and `function`/`file`/`line` when known.

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_FRAME_SCOPE

values.name: STURDY_TRACE_FRAME_UNWOUND

enums.name: SturdyUiDirection

enums.name: SturdyUiGraphType
enums.doc: Chart type for `sturdy_ui_graph_draw`.

enums.name: SturdyUiScaleMode
enums.doc: How UI units map onto the framebuffer.

values.name: STURDY_UI_SCALE_MODE_CONTENT_SCALE
values.doc: One UI unit covers `sturdy_window_content_scale` pixels, so the UI keeps its physical size on every display and text stays sharp. The default.

values.name: STURDY_UI_SCALE_MODE_RAW_PIXELS
values.doc: One UI unit is one framebuffer pixel, whatever the display scale.

enums.doc: How an element sizes itself along one axis.

values.name: STURDY_UI_SIZING_FIT
values.doc: Shrink to fit the children.

values.name: STURDY_UI_SIZING_GROW

values.name: STURDY_UI_SIZING_FIXED

values.name: STURDY_UI_SIZING_PERCENT
values.doc: A fraction of the parent, where `value` is 0..1.

enums.name: SturdyVSync

values.name: STURDY_VSYNC_ADAPTIVE
values.doc: Tears rather than stalling when a frame misses the refresh deadline.

enums.name: SturdyVariableRefreshMode
enums.doc: Variable refresh rate policy. Matches `Core::VariableRefreshMode`.

enums.name: SturdyVertexFormat
enums.doc: Per-vertex-attribute data layout. Ordinal values are pinned to match the engine's internal `RHI::VertexFormat` and must stay in this exact order.

enums.name: SturdyWindowEffectKind
enums.doc: Platform-composited visual effect a window can request. Support is OS-dependent — an effect this platform cannot render (e.g. Mica off Windows 11) is rejected with `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` rather than silently ignored.

enums.name: SturdyWindowMode

enums.name: SturdyWindowRequestKind
enums.doc: Which kind of window request a `SturdyWindowRequestCompletion` reports the outcome of.

values.name: STURDY_WINDOW_REQUEST_CLOSE

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructure
structs.doc: Handle to an acceleration structure. See the "Ray tracing" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureAabbsDesc
structs.doc: Procedural (AABB) geometry within an acceleration structure build.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildDesc
structs.doc: Describes one acceleration structure build (or update, if `src` is nonzero). `geometries` must match what was passed to `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes` when `dst` was sized.

fields.name: src
fields.doc: Zero handle for an initial build; the structure being updated for an in-place update.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildRangeInfo
structs.doc: How many primitives (and at what offsets) each geometry in a build contributes. Index-aligned with the build's `geometries` array.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureBuildSizes
structs.doc: Buffer sizes needed to build an acceleration structure, returned by `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes`.

fields.name: acceleration_structure_size
fields.doc: Pass to `SturdyAccelerationStructureDesc::size`.

fields.name: build_scratch_size
fields.doc: Scratch buffer size needed for an initial build.

fields.name: update_scratch_size
fields.doc: Scratch buffer size needed for an in-place update (only meaningful with `STURDY_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_FLAGS_ALLOW_UPDATE`).

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureDesc
structs.doc: Describes an acceleration structure to create. `size` must come from `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes`.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureGeometryDesc
structs.doc: One geometry entry in an acceleration structure build. `type` selects which of `triangles`/`aabbs`/`instances` is meaningful; the other two are ignored. Mirrors `RHI::AccelerationStructureGeometryDesc`, which carries all three as plain members rather than a tagged union.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance
structs.doc: One row of a top-level acceleration structure's instance buffer. Fixed 64-byte layout matching `VkAccelerationStructureInstanceKHR`/`D3D12_RAYTRACING_INSTANCE_DESC` exactly (and `RHI::AccelerationStructureInstance`) — write an array of these directly into a mapped/staged buffer bound as `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstancesDesc::buffer`.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc: Row-major 3x4 object-to-world transform (3 rows of 4 floats each).

fields.name: custom_index_and_mask
fields.doc: Packed via `sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_custom_index_and_mask`.

fields.name: shader_binding_table_offset_and_flags
fields.doc: Packed via `sturdy_rhi_pack_instance_sbt_offset_and_flags`.

fields.name: acceleration_structure_device_address
fields.doc: From `sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_device_address` on the referenced bottom-level structure.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureInstancesDesc
structs.doc: Top-level instance geometry within an acceleration structure build.

fields.name: buffer
fields.doc: A buffer of `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance` records, or of pointers to them if `array_of_pointers` is set.

structs.name: SturdyAccelerationStructureTrianglesDesc
structs.doc: Triangle geometry within an acceleration structure build. `opacity_micromap` is a zero handle unless `Feature`-gated opacity micromaps are used (Vulkan only).

fields.name: transform_buffer
fields.doc: Zero handle means no per-instance transform.

structs.name: SturdyAdapterInfo
structs.doc:
Numeric identity of the adapter the engine selected.

Text fields (name, vendor, driver version, API version, stable device id) are read separately through `sturdy_rhi_adapter_string`, following the string-output convention above.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyAdapterInfo)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAmbientOcclusionSettings)` by `sturdy_ambient_occlusion_settings_init`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: World-space radius the occlusion search covers around a shaded point.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: Blend toward fully unoccluded. 1 = full strength, 0 = no occlusion.

fields.name: falloff_range
fields.doc: Fraction of `radius` over which an occluder fades out.

fields.name: thin_occluder_compensation
fields.doc: Thin-occluder compensation, in [0, 0.7].

fields.name: final_value_power
fields.doc: Contrast curve applied to the visibility term.

fields.name: sample_distribution_power
fields.doc: Exponent of the normalized sample-distance distribution.

fields.name: denoise
fields.doc: Runs the 5x5 edge-aware spatial denoiser.

structs.name: SturdyAnimationSet
structs.doc: Animation loaded from a file on its own (BVH mocap, or glTF/FBX with no mesh such as Mixamo downloads). Owned: valid until `sturdy_animation_set_release`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAntiAliasingSettings)` by `sturdy_anti_aliasing_settings_init`.

structs.name: SturdyAsset
structs.doc:
An engine asset — a shader, model or texture.

Opaque by value: the bytes are the engine's own asset handle, copied in and out rather than interpreted. Copy it freely, compare it with `memcmp`, and treat a zeroed value as invalid. It stays valid for as long as the engine that produced it.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAudioConfig)`.

fields.name: sample_rate
fields.doc: 0 selects 48000.

fields.name: channel_count
fields.doc: Used with `STURDY_AUDIO_LAYOUT_CHANNEL_COUNT`.

fields.name: max_voices
fields.doc: 0 selects the defaults (8192 voices, 4096 audible at once, helper threads chosen by the engine).

fields.name: open_device
fields.doc: Open the default playback device. False mixes silently (headless tools, tests, or when a custom sink takes the output).

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyAutoExposureSettings)` by `sturdy_auto_exposure_settings_init`.

fields.name: min_log2_luminance
fields.doc: Luminance range the histogram meters, as log2(scene-linear luminance).

fields.name: low_percent
fields.doc: Fractions of the metered pixel mass ignored at the dark / bright end (`0 < = low < high < = 1`).

fields.name: key_value
fields.doc: Luminance the metered average is mapped to (middle grey).

fields.name: compensation_ev
fields.doc: Exposure compensation in stops.

fields.name: adapt_up_speed
fields.doc: Adaptation rates per second when the scene darkens (exposure rises) / brightens.

fields.name: center_weight
fields.doc: 0 = every pixel counts equally, 1 = the frame edges count for nothing.

structs.doc: Describes a bind group layout to create.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyBindGroupLayoutDesc)` by the caller.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.doc: One binding slot within a bind group layout.

structs.name: SturdyEngine
structs.doc:
Borrowed reference to the live engine, valid only inside the callback that received it.

A struct wrapping an integer rather than a raw pointer: the integer is a token that is minted when a callback begins and revoked when it returns, and tokens are never reused. A stale token therefore always resolves to "expired" instead of aliasing a later object.

structs.doc:
Identifies an entity.

Every call below checks the generation and reports `STURDY_ERROR_ENTITY_NOT_ALIVE` rather than acting on the wrong entity. A zeroed `SturdyEntity` is never alive.

structs.name: SturdyGameLogic
structs.doc:
Callbacks implementing your application, mirroring the C++ `Engine::GameLogic` interface.

Every callback may be null; a null callback behaves as a no-op that neither fails nor renders. `user_data` is passed back to each callback untouched and is never interpreted by the engine.

fields.doc: Opaque pointer handed back to every callback below.

fields.name: on_engine_initialized
fields.doc: Called once after the engine and its first window are live, before any frame.

fields.name: request_render_frame
fields.doc:
Called once per frame per surface to describe what should be drawn.

Configure `frame` with the `sturdy_frame_*` setters, then return `STURDY_TRUE` to render it. Return `STURDY_FALSE` to skip this frame entirely — the correct answer when there is nothing new to show, since it presents no frame rather than presenting a blank one.

`frame` arrives pre-populated with the engine's standard render pipeline and a camera whose aspect ratio already matches this surface, so a caller that configures nothing still produces a complete frame. Every setter overrides part of that starting point.

fields.name: on_shutdown
fields.doc: Called once during teardown, before the engine is destroyed. Failures cannot be reported from here; shutdown proceeds regardless.

fields.name: destroy
fields.doc: Called exactly once after `on_shutdown`, to release whatever `user_data` owns. This is the hook a binding uses to drop its language-side object (a boxed Rust struct, a pinned GC handle) at a well-defined point rather than leaking it.

structs.doc:
An imported glTF scene: its models, the node instances that place them, and its lights.

Unlike `SturdyEngine` and `SturdyFrame`, this handle is **owned, not borrowed**. It stays valid until you pass it to `sturdy_gltf_release`, which is the one thing on this ABI you must explicitly free. Releasing it does not destroy the models it produced — those belong to the engine's asset manager and outlive the scene, which is what lets you keep spawning them.

structs.name: SturdyGpuInfo

Unlike other queries in this header, `name`/`vendor`/`physical_device_id` are fixed-size buffers embedded directly in this struct rather than following the general string-output convention above (buffer + capacity + `*out_length`, queried by calling twice): enumeration itself creates and tears down a temporary graphics instance per backend, so asking a second time to learn a string's length would pay that cost again and risks a different snapshot (a GPU unplugged between calls) coming back. Values are always null-terminated, truncated rather than overflowed if a driver-reported string is unusually long.

fields.doc: True for a static data member — access it with `sturdy_reflection_get_static_field`/ `_set_static_field` instead of the instance versions.

fields.name: is_read_only
fields.doc: True when the field rejects writes (`sturdy_reflection_set_field` returns `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`).

fields.name: is_container
fields.doc: True when the field is a recognized container (`std::vector <T >` with a trivially-copyable `T`, in the current engine) — see the container section below.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionId
structs.doc: Identifies a reflected type, field, method, event, or enum. Derived from its canonical name and stable for the process lifetime (or until unregistered) — the same shape as `SturdyResourceId`, since both wrap the engine's underlying 128-bit name hash identically.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionMethodInfo
structs.doc: What the engine knows about a reflected method.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyReflectionMethodInfo)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: is_static
fields.doc: True for a static member function — call it with `sturdy_reflection_invoke_static_method` instead of the instance version.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionSettings
structs.doc: Indirect specular light (since 0.33): the sky prefiltered per roughness (so every surface reflects something and metals are never black) plus deterministic (noise-free) screen-space reflections with cone-traced glossiness, which replace it where the reflected surface is on screen. On by default.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyReflectionSettings)` by `sturdy_reflection_settings_init`.

fields.name: max_roughness
fields.doc: Surfaces rougher than this (perceptual roughness) use only the environment.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc: How far behind the depth buffer a surface is assumed to extend, as a fraction of its view depth.

fields.name: glossy_blur
fields.doc: Scales how fast the specular cone widens with distance (1 = the GGX lobe).

structs.name: SturdyReflectionSubscription
structs.doc: Handle to an installed before-hook/after-hook/event-listener subscription, for later removal with the matching `_remove_*`/`_unsubscribe_event` call. Not scope-bound — stays valid until explicitly removed or the type it was installed on is unregistered.

structs.name: SturdyReflectionTypeBuilder
structs.doc: Handle to an in-progress type description. Owned by the caller — build it up with the `_add_*` calls below, then either `_finish` it (consuming the builder, registering the type) or `_discard` it (consuming the builder without registering anything).

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundle
structs.doc: Handle to a finished, replayable render bundle. Unlike the encoder that produced it, this carries no scope of its own — like `SturdyBuffer`, it is an informational identifier the RHI device owns and validates until `sturdy_rhi_destroy_render_bundle`.

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundleDesc
structs.doc: Describes a render bundle to create. Bundles are format-only — they record against whatever render pass later executes them, matching it by attachment formats/sample count/view mask rather than by binding real attachments.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderBundleDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_desc_init`.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: Sample count as an integer (1, 2, 4, 8, or 16), matching `RHI::SampleCount`'s values.

fields.name: label

structs.name: SturdyRenderBundleEncoder
structs.doc: Owned handle to an in-progress bundle recording, borrowed from the engine's active device. Lives until `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_finish` or `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_release`.

structs.doc: Owned handle to an in-progress render pass, borrowed from its command encoder. Lives until `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end`. The parent `SturdyCommandEncoder` may not be used for anything else while a pass is open.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPipeline
structs.doc: Handle to a render pipeline. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyRenderPipelineDesc
structs.doc:
Everything needed to build a raster pipeline against dynamic rendering (no render-pass object). Viewport/scissor are always dynamic, set per-draw on the render pass encoder, so they are not part of this description. All array fields are read synchronously during `sturdy_rhi_create_render_pipeline` and need not outlive the call.

Set `mesh` (and optionally `task`) for a mesh-shader pipeline, or set `vertex` for a traditional vertex-input pipeline — not both. A mesh pipeline requires the `"mesh shaders"` feature (check with `sturdy_rhi_feature_index`/`sturdy_rhi_feature_enabled`) and ignores `vertex_buffers`/`topology`; a task stage additionally requires `"task/amplification shaders"`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderPipelineDesc)` by `sturdy_rhi_render_pipeline_desc_init`.

fields.name: fragment
fields.doc: Module may be the zero handle for a depth-only pipeline.

fields.name: depth_stencil
fields.doc: `format` field `STURDY_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` means no depth/stencil attachment.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

fields.name: task
fields.doc: Amplification/task stage for a mesh-shader pipeline. Zero handle means no task stage.

fields.name: mesh
fields.doc: Mesh stage. A valid (nonzero) module here selects the mesh-shader pipeline path instead of `vertex`.

structs.name: SturdyRenderTextureDesc
structs.doc:
Describes a texture built directly from raw pixels, for `sturdy_render_create_texture`.

Named distinctly from the RHI-level `SturdyTextureDesc` (see "RHI resources" below) even though both describe "a texture to create": that one configures a raw GPU resource (`SturdyFormat`, mip levels, usage flags, no pixel data), while this one is the asset-manager-level counterpart to `sturdy_render_load_texture` — pixels in, a `SturdyAsset` usable with `sturdy_render_set_model_texture` out.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRenderTextureDesc)` by `sturdy_render_texture_desc_init`.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Capped well below any real GPU's maximum, only to keep `width * height * 4` from overflowing while validating this struct — the real limit is `SturdyDeviceLimits::max_texture_dimension_2d`.

fields.name: rgba8
fields.doc: RGBA8 pixel data, `width * height * 4` bytes, row-major and tightly packed (no row padding). Copied before this call returns; the pointer need not outlive it.

structs.name: SturdyResourceId
structs.doc: Identifies a resource or event type. Derived from its canonical name and stable across runs.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRestirGiSettings)` by `sturdy_restir_gi_settings_init`.

fields.name: multi_bounce_feedback
fields.doc: Damping (0-1) applied to last frame's lit scene color when read back as an extra indirect term. 0 disables multi-bounce feedback.

fields.name: svgf_atrous_iterations
fields.doc: Only read when `denoiser` is `STURDY_RESTIR_GI_DENOISER_SVGF`.

structs.name: SturdyRuntimeConfig
structs.doc:
Application and window configuration for `sturdy_runtime_run`.

Populate with `sturdy_runtime_config_init` first — that sets `struct_size` and every default — then override only the fields you care about. String fields are borrowed UTF-8 and must stay alive for the duration of the `sturdy_runtime_run` call; the engine copies what it needs.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyRuntimeConfig)`. `sturdy_runtime_config_init` does this for you.

fields.name: app_name
fields.doc: Application name reported to the graphics driver. Null selects the engine default.

fields.name: window_title
fields.doc: Initial title of the primary window. Null selects the engine default.

fields.name: shaders_directory
fields.doc: Directory the engine loads shaders from, relative to the working directory unless absolute. Null selects `"Shaders"`.

fields.name: window_width
fields.doc: Primary window client-area size in physical pixels.

fields.name: enable_raytracing
fields.doc: Request ray-tracing support at device creation. Initialization fails if the selected adapter cannot provide it, rather than silently continuing without — features that depend on it (ReSTIR GI) would otherwise fail confusingly at first use.

fields.name: enable_shader_disk_cache
fields.doc: Cache compiled shaders on disk between runs.

fields.name: enable_native_access
fields.doc: Publish the backend's raw Vulkan or D3D12 objects, making the `sturdy_native_*` family usable. Off by default and opt-in on purpose: it is the one part of this ABI that hands out pointers the engine's own invariants do not cover, so a build that never asks for it cannot accidentally come to depend on native access.

fields.name: physical_device_id
fields.doc:
Selects a specific GPU by the stable identifier reported through `STURDY_ADAPTER_STRING_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_ID`. Null or empty lets the engine pick.

This is the other half of persisting a user's GPU choice: read the id from a previous run's adapter, store it, and pass it back here. Identifiers agree across Vulkan and D3D12 for the same physical device, so a choice made under one backend still resolves under the other.

An id that matches no device on this machine **fails startup** with `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` rather than quietly selecting a different GPU — the engine treats an explicit device request as a requirement, not a hint. Hardware does change between runs, so an application persisting this value should be prepared to clear it and retry with null once, instead of treating the failure as fatal.

structs.name: SturdySampler

fields.name: temporal_alpha

fields.name: max_radiance

structs.name: SturdySemaphore
structs.doc: Handle to a timeline semaphore: a GPU-to-GPU (and GPU-to-host, via `sturdy_rhi_wait_semaphore`) synchronization primitive that counts up through a sequence of `u64` values rather than toggling once like a fence. Reach for this to order work across two queues (e.g. an upload on the transfer queue that a graphics-queue submission must wait on); use `SturdyFence` instead for the common "wait for this one submission to finish on the host" case. See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdySemaphoreDesc

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Optional debug label, copied at creation time. May be null.

structs.doc: One semaphore a submission waits on before its work begins.

structs.name: SturdyShaderBindingTableRegion
structs.doc: One shader binding table region: a byte range in a buffer holding shader group handles written by `sturdy_rhi_write_ray_tracing_shader_group_handles`. `stride` is ignored for `raygen` (a single record); `miss`/`hit`/`callable` are strided tables.

structs.name: SturdyShaderEntry

structs.name: SturdyShaderModule

See the "RHI resources" section header for its lifetime rules.

structs.name: SturdyShaderModuleDesc
structs.doc: Describes a shader module to create from raw bytecode.

structs.name: SturdyShapeParams

Dimensions for a built-in shape. Only the fields listed for the chosen shape are read.

Initialize with `sturdy_render_shape_params_init`, which fills the same defaults the engine's C++ primitives use, then override what you care about.

structs.name: SturdyStencilFaceState
structs.doc: Stencil behavior for one face (front or back).

structs.name: SturdySurface
structs.doc:
Identifies the render surface (window) a frame is being produced for.

Opaque and informational in this ABI version: use it to tell surfaces apart across callbacks when an application has multiple windows. It carries no lifetime of its own.

structs.name: SturdySystem
structs.doc: Handle to a system registered through `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex`.

structs.name: SturdySystemAccess
structs.doc: One component a system operates on, and how.

structs.name: SturdySystemResourceAccess
structs.doc: One resource or event channel a system operates on, and how.

structs.name: SturdyTask
structs.doc:
A running background task.

Owned like `SturdyGltfScene`, not scope-bound: it stays valid until `sturdy_async_release`. Releasing does **not** cancel the task — there is no cancellation — it only says you are done observing it. A task whose handle has been released still runs to completion, so whatever its `user_data` points at must stay alive until the task itself finishes.

structs.name: SturdyVulkanHandles
structs.doc:
The engine's raw Vulkan objects.

**Every handle is borrowed.** The engine owns them and destroys them at shutdown. Do not destroy them, and do not use them after the engine is gone. Anything you do with them sits outside the engine's own synchronization: if you submit work on these queues or record into the device, you are responsible for not racing the engine's frame loop.

structs.name: SturdyWebGpuHandles
structs.doc:
The engine's raw WebGPU objects.

Fields are `void *` for the same reason as `SturdyVulkanHandles`/`SturdyD3D12Handles`, and carry the same borrowing rules. Unlike those two, this deliberately stops at the WebGPU objects themselves rather than reaching beneath them to whatever native API Dawn chose (Vulkan, Metal, or D3D12) -- that is fundamentally unavailable on the Web target (a browser's WebGPU implementation exposes no native handles to any embedder) and would defeat the point of the backend even on native Dawn. Cast each field to its documented `webgpu.h` type. There is exactly one queue: WebGPU has no separate graphics/compute/transfer queues to distinguish, so there is no `sturdy_native_webgpu_queue` counterpart to `sturdy_native_vulkan_queue`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyWebGpuHandles)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: instance
fields.doc: `WGPUInstance`.

fields.name: adapter
fields.doc: `WGPUAdapter`.

fields.name: device
fields.doc: `WGPUDevice`.

fields.name: queue
fields.doc: `WGPUQueue`, the one queue every WebGPU device exposes.

structs.name: SturdyWindowConfig
structs.doc: Configuration for a new window, as handed to `sturdy_window_spawn` / `sturdy_window_recreate_primary`. The window's graphics API always matches the engine's active backend — there is no field for it here, since a second window using a different backend is not something this engine supports.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set to `sizeof(SturdyWindowConfig)` by `sturdy_window_config_init`.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: Copied by the engine before this call returns; the pointer need not outlive it. Null means "Sturdy Engine".

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Client-area size in physical pixels on every platform.

fields.name: use_default_position
fields.doc: When true, `position_x`/`position_y` are ignored and the OS picks a placement.

fields.name: high_dpi
fields.doc: Whether the window should render at the display's native pixel density rather than being upscaled. `SturdyWindowSnapshot::framebuffer_width/height` reflects the actual result.

structs.name: SturdyWindowRequestCompletion
structs.doc: Outcome of one completed window request: `sturdy_window_spawn`, `sturdy_window_recreate_primary`, or `sturdy_window_request_close`.

fields.name: request_id
fields.doc: Matches the `out_request_id` the originating call produced.

fields.name: accepted
fields.doc: False when the request failed (window creation refused by the platform, runtime window management disabled, or a close naming a window that no longer exists); `surface` is not valid in that case.

structs.name: SturdyWindowSnapshot
structs.doc:
Observed state of one window this frame.

`width`/`height` are window coordinates (the space mouse positions and `position_x/y` use) and `framebuffer_width/height` are physical pixels. They are equal on Windows/X11 and differ on macOS, scaled Wayland and the Web. Render with the framebuffer values. The display's UI scale is separate; read it with `sturdy_window_content_scale`.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.doc: Set by the engine to `sizeof(SturdyWindowSnapshot)` as this build sees it.

fields.name: surface_id
fields.doc: Matches the `SturdySurface::id` handed to `request_render_frame`, so a frame callback can look up the window it is drawing into.

callbacks.name: SturdyAudioSinkCallback
callbacks.doc: Receives mixed audio from a custom sink. Runs on a thread of the engine's, never the audio thread; `interleaved` holds `frames * channels` floats and is only valid during the call.

callbacks.name: SturdyChunkSystemFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a system registered with `sturdy_ecs_add_chunk_system_ex` (since 0.35): called once per matching archetype with that archetype's contiguous arrays, instead of once per entity.

`entities` holds `count` entities. `columns[i]` is the first element of an array of `count` components, one array per entry of the access list in the order it was given, each element as large as that component's size; element `r` of every array belongs to `entities[r]`. Write through the arrays declared `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE`. All pointers are valid only for this call. `commands` is as for `SturdySystemFn`.

One call crosses the language boundary for a whole archetype, so a system over 10,000 entities costs a few calls instead of 10,000: use this for anything per-frame over many entities.

callbacks.name: SturdyEcsVisitFn
callbacks.doc:
Receives one matching entity during `sturdy_ecs_for_each`.

`components` points at an array parallel to the component ids you asked to match, each entry addressing that component's storage for this entity. Write through them to mutate in place. The pointers are valid only for the duration of this call.

While a visit is in progress the world is locked, so this callback must **not** call any other `sturdy_ecs_*` function; each returns `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY`. That guard is doing real work — the engine underneath treats a structural change made during iteration as a fatal contract violation, so without it a reentrant spawn would terminate the process rather than fail. Read and write through `components`; if you need to spawn or destroy, record what you want and do it after `sturdy_ecs_for_each` returns.

callbacks.name: SturdyLogCallback
callbacks.doc: Invoked once per log message after registration via `sturdy_log_add_sink`.

callbacks.name: SturdyPluginEntryFn
callbacks.doc: The one function a plugin exports, under the name `sturdy_plugin_entry`. Return `STURDY_OK` to accept the load; anything else aborts it, destroys any modules already added, and `UNLOAD` is *not* called. For `UNLOAD`, `host->context` is valid but `add_module` is refused, and `state` carries what the plugin stored.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionFieldGetFn
callbacks.doc: Same shape as `SturdyReflectionMethodFn`'s two data-access halves — a non-`Trivial` field's copy-out implementation, called with `object` = the field-owning instance.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionMethodFn
callbacks.doc: A type-erased method call/override/hook body: `object` is the receiver (null for a static method), `args` is one already-typed, caller-marshalled pointer per parameter (see `SturdyReflectionMethodInfo::param_count`), `out_return` is uninitialized storage for the return value (ignored when the method returns nothing), `user_data` is whatever was passed to `sturdy_reflection_register_override`.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionMoveConstructFn
callbacks.doc: Sets the construct/destroy callbacks for the type being built.

callbacks.name: SturdyReflectionObserverFn
callbacks.doc: A type-erased *observer* body — used for both a method before/after hook and an event listener, which share this exact shape (unlike `SturdyReflectionMethodFn`, there is no `out_return`: neither a hook nor an event listener produces a value, only observes `args`). `object` is the method's receiver (null for a static method) or whatever `sturdy_reflection_fire_event` was called with; `args` is one already-typed pointer per parameter; `user_data` is whatever was passed to `_add_before_hook`/`_add_after_hook`/ `_subscribe_event`.

callbacks.name: SturdySystemFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a system registered with `sturdy_ecs_add_system`.

`components` points at an array parallel to the access list the system was registered with, each entry addressing that component's storage for this entity. Write through the ones declared `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE`; the pointers are valid only for this call.

`commands` queues spawns, destroys and component changes for the engine to apply once the stage finishes. That indirection is not optional — the world cannot be restructured while systems are reading it, which is why the direct `sturdy_ecs_spawn` family reports `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` here.

callbacks.name: SturdyTaskFn
callbacks.doc:
Body of a background task.

Runs on a scheduler worker thread, not the thread that spawned it. Must not unwind.

Nothing in this ABI is safe to call concurrently with the engine's own frame from a worker thread — the ECS and renderer entry points assume the caller is the thread the engine handed a handle to. Use tasks for work that does not touch the engine (loading, decoding, pathfinding, network), publish the result somewhere your game logic reads, and apply it from a system or frame callback.

functions.name: sturdy_async_is_done
functions.doc:
Reports whether a task has finished.

The non-blocking way to observe one: poll this from your frame callback rather than waiting.

functions.name: sturdy_async_is_running
functions.doc:
Reports whether the engine's task scheduler is running.

It starts on first use — the first frame or the first `sturdy_async_spawn` — so this reads false before then.

functions.name: sturdy_async_is_worker_thread
functions.doc:
Reports whether the calling thread is a scheduler worker.

Worth checking before doing anything that blocks: blocking a worker starves the pool it belongs to.

functions.name: sturdy_async_release
functions.doc:
Releases a task handle.

Does not cancel or wait. Releasing before the task finishes is fine and is the normal thing to do for fire-and-forget work; the task keeps running.

Releasing twice reports `STURDY_ERROR_HANDLE_EXPIRED`, since task tokens are never reused.

functions.name: sturdy_async_spawn
functions.doc:
Runs `task` on a background thread.

Starts the scheduler if it is not already running.

params.name: task
params.doc: Body to run. Must not be null and must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed to `task` untouched. Must stay alive until the task completes, which is not the same as until the handle is released.

params.name: weight
params.doc: Whether this is short or long work.

params.name: out_task
params.doc: Receives the task handle. May be null if you never need to observe it — the task still runs, and nothing needs releasing.

functions.name: sturdy_async_wait
functions.doc:
Blocks until a task finishes.

Reports `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` when called from a scheduler worker thread. Waiting there can deadlock — the task you are waiting for may be queued behind you on the very pool you are occupying — so it is refused rather than risked.

functions.name: sturdy_async_worker_count
functions.doc:
Returns how many worker threads the scheduler has.

Zero when it is not running. Useful for sizing your own work splitting to the machine.
