functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_chunk_system_ex
functions.doc: Registers a chunk system (since 0.35) with a removable handle. Declaration, ordering, conflict detection, `commands` and removal behave exactly as for `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex`; only the body differs.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components to iterate. At least one is required: a chunk system always iterates, and a system with nothing to iterate belongs on `sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex` as a global system.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run. Must not unwind.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_component
functions.doc: Attaches a component to an existing entity.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_PRESENT` if the entity already carries it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system
functions.doc:
Registers a system that runs every frame, once per entity carrying all the listed components.

The access list is what makes automatic parallelism safe. A C++ system declares its access through its parameter types and the engine derives the rest; a function pointer carries no such information, so you declare it here. The scheduler then orders systems so that nothing writing a component runs alongside anything else touching it, and lets non-conflicting systems run together.

**Declaring less access than you take is the one way to get data races.** If a system might write a component, declare `STURDY_ACCESS_WRITE` even when it usually only reads — an over-declared system costs parallelism, an under-declared one costs correctness.

Systems stay registered for the life of the engine; there is no removal yet.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components the system operates on and how. Must be non-empty, at most 16, and free of duplicates.

params.name: access_count
params.doc: How many entries `access` has.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run per entity. Must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `system` untouched.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK` once registered. The system first runs on the next frame.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system_ex
functions.doc: Like `sturdy_ecs_add_system_with_resources`, but returns a handle so the system can later be removed, disabled, or ordered. Use this when the system's `user_data` is owned by something that can be destroyed (a script VM, a closure): remove the system first, then free the data.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_system_with_resources
functions.doc:
Registers a system that also touches resources or event channels.

The component half behaves exactly as `sturdy_ecs_add_system`. The resource half is what lets the scheduler order a foreign system against systems — C++ or otherwise — that use the same resources: two systems writing the same resource will not run concurrently, and a reader will not overlap a writer.

Passing zero components registers a **global** system: with nothing to iterate, the body runs exactly once per frame, with a default-constructed entity and a null component array. That is the right shape for a system that only drains an event channel or advances a resource.

params.name: access
params.doc: Components the system operates on. May be null when `access_count` is zero.

params.name: access_count
params.doc: How many entries `access` has. At most 16.

params.name: resource_access
params.doc: Resources and event channels the system operates on. May be null when `resource_access_count` is zero.

params.name: resource_access_count
params.doc: How many entries `resource_access` has.

params.name: system
params.doc: Body to run. Must not unwind.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `system` untouched.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_add_tag
functions.doc:
Attaches a tag component to an entity.

A convenience over `sturdy_ecs_add_component` that supplies the byte for you, since a tag has no value to pass.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_PRESENT` if the entity already carries it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_clear_events
functions.doc:
Discards every event currently buffered on a channel.

Rarely needed: the engine drains channels once per frame on its own. Use this when a channel is filled and consumed entirely within one frame and should not be seen again.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_add_component
functions.doc: Queues attaching a component, applied after the current stage finishes.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_destroy
functions.doc: Queues destruction of an entity, applied after the current stage finishes.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_remove_component
functions.doc: Queues detaching a component, applied after the current stage finishes.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_commands_spawn
functions.doc: Queues creation of an entity, applied after the current stage finishes.

params.name: commands
params.doc: Handle supplied to your system.

params.name: components
params.doc: Initial value for each component; copied immediately, so your storage need not outlive this call.

params.name: component_count
params.doc: How many entries `components` has.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field
functions.doc: Reads field `index`, in the order the fields were registered in.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is not below `sturdy_ecs_component_field_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field_count
functions.doc: How many fields a component was registered with (since 0.35); 0 when its registrant did not describe them.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_field_name
functions.doc: Reads field `index`'s name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a component.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_layout_fingerprint
functions.doc: The 128-bit fingerprint of a component's registered layout (size, alignment, every field's kind, offset and count), as two words; both zero when its registrant did not describe the fields. Lets a binding compare against a value baked in at build time without re-implementing the hash.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_component_name
functions.doc: Reads a component's canonical name. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel
functions.doc:
Creates an event channel: a buffer of fixed-size records the engine drains every frame.

Events differ from resources in exactly that draining. Anything sent during a frame is readable for the rest of that frame and gone by the next, which is what makes them the right way to communicate between systems without either one owning the data.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name such as `"mygame.damage_event"`.

params.name: event_size
params.doc: Byte size of one event. Must be nonzero.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the channel identifier. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel_ex
functions.doc:
Like `sturdy_ecs_create_event_channel`, additionally describing the event payload's fields (since 0.35).

An event channel is how two modules written in different languages talk to each other, so they must agree on the payload. `desc->size` is the event size and `align` is ignored. Creating the channel again under the same name must give the same size and, when both calls describe their fields, the same layout (kinds, offsets, counts; names are ignored); a mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and names the first field that differs.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_resource
functions.doc:
Creates a resource, taking ownership of its storage.

The engine's own resources are bound by reference to storage their C++ owner keeps alive. A foreign caller has no comparable place to put that storage, so the engine allocates and owns it here, zero-initialized or copied from `initial_data`. It lives until `sturdy_ecs_destroy_resource` or process exit.

Binding a name that already exists rebinds nothing and succeeds, provided the size matches; a different size under the same name is rejected, because anything already reading it expects the old layout.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name.

params.name: size
params.doc: Byte size. Must be nonzero.

params.name: initial_data
params.doc: Initial value, or null to zero-initialize.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the resource identifier. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_create_resource_ex
functions.doc: Like `sturdy_ecs_create_resource`, additionally describing the value's fields (since 0.35).

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, `size` and fields, as for `sturdy_ecs_register_component_ex`; `align` is ignored (the engine allocates the storage). Re-creating a resource under the same name must give the same size and, when both calls describe their fields, the same layout: two languages that share a resource must agree on what is in it, not just how big it is. A mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and names the first field that differs.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_destroy
functions.doc: Destroys an entity. Destroying an already-dead entity is a no-op, not an error, so cleanup code does not have to track whether it already ran.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_destroy_resource
functions.doc: Destroys a resource created through `sturdy_ecs_create_resource` and frees its storage.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is bound under that id, or when it is bound to storage this ABI does not own — the engine's own C++ resources cannot be destroyed here.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_event_count
functions.doc: Returns how many events are currently buffered on a channel.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_find_component
functions.doc:
Looks up a component id by canonical name.

Also the way to reach the engine's own components — `"sturdy.engine.world_transform"` and the rest — without registering anything.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is registered under that name.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_for_each
functions.doc:
Visits every live entity carrying all of the listed components.

This is the query primitive: the engine walks only the archetypes that match, so cost scales with matching entities rather than with the whole world.

params.name: components
params.doc: Components an entity must all carry to be visited. At most 16.

params.name: component_count
params.doc: How many entries `components` has.

params.name: visit
params.doc: Invoked once per matching entity. Must not unwind, and must not call back into `sturdy_ecs_*` — see `SturdyEcsVisitFn`.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Passed through to `visit` untouched.

params.name: out_visited
params.doc: Receives how many entities were visited. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_get_component
functions.doc:
Copies a component's current value out.

A copy rather than a pointer: component storage moves when entities gain or lose components, so a pointer handed across the boundary would go stale in a way the caller could not detect.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size. A mismatch is rejected rather than partially copied, because it means your struct and the engine's disagree.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_get_resource
functions.doc: Copies a resource's current value out.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the resource's byte size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is bound under that id.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_has_component
functions.doc: Reports whether an entity carries a component. A dead entity reports false rather than failing.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_has_resource
functions.doc: Reports whether a resource is bound.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_is_alive
functions.doc: Reports whether an entity is alive.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_order_system_after
functions.doc: Forces `system` to run in a later stage than `dependency`, in addition to whatever ordering the declared access already implies. A cycle aborts when the schedule is next built.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_read_event
functions.doc: Copies one buffered event out of a channel.

params.name: index
params.doc: Event to read, less than `sturdy_ecs_event_count`.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the channel's event size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_component
functions.doc:
Registers a plain-data component type, or returns the existing id if one is already registered under that name.

The component is treated as raw bytes: copied with the equivalent of `memcpy` and destroyed with no cleanup. That is why only plain data works here — a foreign caller has no way to supply C++ construction and destruction semantics, so anything owning a resource must be defined in C++.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name. Use a namespaced form such as `"mygame.health"`; the engine derives a stable key from it, so it must not collide with another component.

params.name: size
params.doc: Bytes per instance. Must be nonzero; use `sturdy_ecs_register_tag_component` for a component that carries no data.

params.name: align
params.doc: Required alignment in bytes. Must be a power of two and at most 64.

params.name: out_component
params.doc: Receives the id.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`. Re-registering the same name with the same layout returns the original id; re-registering it with a *different* layout is rejected, since existing storage and existing entities are already laid out the old way.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_component_ex
functions.doc:
Registers a component and its field layout (since 0.35), so languages sharing it can be checked against each other.

Behaves like `sturdy_ecs_register_component` (same name and layout returns the existing id; a different size or alignment is rejected), and additionally: the fields must fit inside `size` and not overlap, and when this registration and an earlier one of the same name both describe their fields, they must describe the same layout (kinds, offsets, counts; field names are ignored). A mismatch fails with `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` and a message naming the first field that differs, so a Rust `{f32, f32}` and a C# `{u32, u32}` cannot silently share an 8-byte component. A registration that gives no fields is still accepted against any layout.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_register_tag_component
functions.doc:
Registers a tag component: one that marks an entity without carrying data.

Tags are for querying — "is this entity a player", "is this one asleep" — where the answer is the presence of the component itself. Add and remove them with `sturdy_ecs_add_tag` and `sturdy_ecs_remove_component`, and match them in `sturdy_ecs_for_each` like any other component.

A tag occupies **one byte**, not zero, because that is what an empty struct occupies in C++ and this ABI does not invent a different layout. The pointer a tag yields during iteration is valid but meaningless; there is nothing to read from it.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name.

params.name: out_component
params.doc: Receives the id.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`. Re-registering an existing tag returns the original id.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_remove_component
functions.doc: Detaches a component from an entity.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_COMPONENT_MISSING` if the entity does not carry it, or `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` if it is the entity's last component — destroy the entity instead of emptying it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_remove_system
functions.doc: Unregisters a system. After this returns the engine no longer references its `user_data`. Fails with `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` semantics (a contract violation) if called while a schedule is running, including from inside a system.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_resource_id
functions.doc:
Derives the identifier for a canonical resource or event name.

Pure and engine-independent, so a binding can compute its ids once at load time. The same name always yields the same id, which is what lets a foreign caller name a resource the engine's own C++ code also uses.

params.name: name
params.doc: Canonical, globally unique name such as `"mygame.score"`.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the identifier.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_send_event
functions.doc: Appends one event to a channel.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the channel's event size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_set_component
functions.doc: Overwrites a component's value in place.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the component's registered size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_set_resource
functions.doc: Overwrites a resource's value.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the resource's byte size.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_set_system_enabled
functions.doc: Skips (or resumes) a system without unregistering it.

functions.name: sturdy_ecs_spawn
functions.doc: Creates an entity carrying the supplied components.

params.name: components
params.doc: Initial value for each component. Must be non-empty and free of duplicates — an entity must carry at least one component.

params.name: component_count
params.doc: How many entries `components` has.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the new entity.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_down
functions.doc: Reports whether a key is currently held.

params.name: key
params.doc: Engine key code. Printable ASCII maps to its own character value; see the engine's `WindowManager::KeyboardKey` for the full set. Out-of-range codes report not-held rather than failing, so a caller mapping from another platform's key enum cannot fault here.

params.name: out_down
params.doc: Receives nonzero when held. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_just_pressed
functions.doc: Reports whether a key transitioned to held during this tick.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_key_just_released
functions.doc: Reports whether a key transitioned to released during this tick.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_mouse_delta
functions.doc:
Reads cursor movement accumulated during this tick.

This is the value to integrate for camera look, not the difference between successive `sturdy_engine_mouse_position` reads: it accumulates every motion event the platform delivered this tick, so it stays correct at high polling rates where several events land per frame.

params.name: out_x
params.doc: Receives horizontal movement. May be null.

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives vertical movement. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_mouse_down
functions.doc: Reports whether a mouse button is currently held.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_mouse_position
functions.doc: Reads the cursor position in window coordinates.

params.name: out_x
params.doc: Receives the horizontal position. May be null.

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives the vertical position. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_engine_wheel_delta
functions.doc: Reads scroll-wheel movement accumulated during this tick.

params.name: out_x
params.doc: Receives horizontal scroll. May be null.

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives vertical scroll. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_camera_look_at
functions.doc: Points the camera at a world-space target, keeping `+Y` as up.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_ambient_light
functions.doc: Sets uniform ambient radiance and the scene exposure multiplier.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_ambient_occlusion_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the ambient-occlusion stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_anti_aliasing_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the anti-aliasing stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_auto_exposure_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the histogram auto-exposure stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_background_color
functions.doc: Sets the color the scene is cleared to, as linear RGBA.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_bloom_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the bloom stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_emulation_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the camera-emulation stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_perspective
functions.doc: Sets a perspective projection.

params.name: vertical_fov_degrees
params.doc: Vertical field of view. Must be in (0, 180).

params.name: near_clip
params.doc: Near plane distance. Must be greater than 0 and less than `far_clip`.

params.name: far_clip
params.doc: Far plane distance.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_position
functions.doc: Places the camera at a world-space position.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_camera_viewport
functions.doc:
Sets the camera's aspect ratio from a viewport size in pixels.

Pass the `framebuffer_width`/`framebuffer_height` from this frame's `SturdyFrameInput` unless you are deliberately rendering at a different aspect. Both must be nonzero.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_color_grade_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the colour-grade settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_debug_label
functions.doc: Attaches a debug label to this frame, surfaced in graphics debuggers and engine logs.

params.name: label
params.doc: Null-terminated UTF-8, or null to clear. Copied; need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_depth_of_field_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the depth-of-field settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_feature_enabled
functions.doc: Enables or disables one render-graph stage for this frame.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_lighting_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the clustered-lighting settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_motion_blur_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the motion-blur stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_reflection_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the reflection settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_resolution_scale
functions.doc: Scales the internal render resolution relative to the surface. Must be in (0, 2].

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_restir_gi_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the ReSTIR GI stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_scene_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the scene stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_screen_space_gi_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the screen-space GI stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_shadow_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the shadow stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_tone_mapping
functions.doc: Selects the tone-mapping operator and its exposure/white-point/saturation controls.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_tone_mapping_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the tone-mapping stage's settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_frame_set_volumetric_fog_settings
functions.doc: Replaces the volumetric-fog settings for the frame being built.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_import
functions.doc:
Imports a glTF or GLB file, creating a model asset for every mesh it contains.

Importing does not put anything in the world — it produces assets and a description of how the file arranged them. Call `sturdy_gltf_spawn_all` to reproduce that arrangement, or walk the instances yourself if you want to filter or re-place them.

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to a `.gltf` or `.glb` file. A `.gltf` referencing external buffers and images resolves them relative to its own directory, so move the whole folder together.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader every imported model draws with. Load one with `sturdy_render_load_shader`.

params.name: out_scene
params.doc: Receives the scene handle. Release it with `sturdy_gltf_release`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_at
functions.doc: Reads the node instance at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_count
functions.doc: Returns how many node instances the scene places.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_instance_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the node instance at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_at
functions.doc: Reads the light at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_count
functions.doc: Returns how many lights the scene declares.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_light_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the light at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_model_at
functions.doc: Reads the model asset at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_model_count
functions.doc: Returns how many distinct models the import produced.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_release
functions.doc:
Releases an imported scene.

Frees the instance and light lists this ABI is holding. The model assets survive — they belong to the asset manager — so anything already spawned keeps rendering.

Releasing twice reports `STURDY_ERROR_HANDLE_EXPIRED` rather than corrupting anything, since scene tokens are never reused.

functions.name: sturdy_gltf_spawn_all
functions.doc:
Spawns an entity for every instance and light in the scene, reproducing it as authored.

The convenience path: import, spawn, release. Instances with no model are skipped, since an entity that draws nothing and lights nothing would only cost iteration.

params.name: out_spawned
params.doc: Receives how many entities were created. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_gpu_enumerate
functions.doc: Enumerates every physical GPU this machine can create an engine on, across every graphics backend this build supports. Safe to call before `sturdy_runtime_run`, with no window or device yet — this is how an application builds its own GPU picker rather than guessing at `physical_device_id` values. Not free: it creates and immediately destroys a temporary graphics instance per backend, so call it once and cache the result rather than every frame.

params.name: out_gpus
params.doc: Copies up to `capacity` entries here.

params.name: capacity
params.doc: Size of `out_gpus`, in entries. May be 0 to just read `*out_count`.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives the true number of GPUs found, which may exceed `capacity` — realistically never more than a handful, so a generously sized buffer (8) avoids this.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_message
functions.doc: Detail for the most recent failing call **on the calling thread**.
functions.returns: A null-terminated UTF-8 string, never null; empty when the last call succeeded. The pointer stays valid until the next ABI call on this same thread, so copy it if you need to keep it. Never freed by the caller.
notes: Thread-local by design: engine frames can run on their own render threads, so a process-wide error slot would let one thread's failure overwrite another's.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_format
functions.doc: The whole trace as readable text, one frame per line, with the usual size-query convention (see `copy_string_out` in the ABI notes: pass a null buffer to learn the size; a short buffer gets a truncated, terminated result and `STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`).

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_frame
functions.doc: Reads one frame of the trace counted by `sturdy_last_error_trace_frame_count`, innermost first.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is past the end.

functions.name: sturdy_last_error_trace_frame_count
functions.doc: Number of frames in the calling thread's most recent trace (the last failure's, or the last `sturdy_trace_capture`). Zero if none. Call this before `sturdy_last_error_trace_frame`: it resolves the trace once so the frames can be read cheaply.

functions.name: sturdy_lighting_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (clustered on).

functions.name: sturdy_log_add_sink
functions.doc: Registers a callback to receive every subsequent log message.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Function invoked per message. Must not be null.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Opaque pointer passed back to `callback` unchanged. May be null.

params.name: out_sink
params.doc: Receives a handle to unregister this sink later with `sturdy_log_remove_sink`.

functions.name: sturdy_log_remove_sink
functions.doc: Unregisters a sink added by `sturdy_log_add_sink`. A null/zero handle, or one already removed, is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_model_import
functions.doc: Imports a model file of any supported format, chosen from its extension: `.gltf`/`.glb`, `.fbx`, `.obj`. Same ownership and release rules as `sturdy_gltf_import`; the handle works with every `sturdy_gltf_*` call.

functions.name: sturdy_module_count
functions.doc: How many modules are loaded.

functions.name: sturdy_module_name
functions.doc: The name of the module at `index` in start order. See the string-output convention above.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index` is not below `sturdy_module_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_load
functions.doc: Adds and starts a module in the running game, after the modules in `module->after` (which must already be loaded).

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_reload
functions.doc: Replaces the module called `name` with `logic`, in the same place in the start order and with the same options. The old module is shut down and its registrations removed first. If `logic`'s `on_engine_initialized` returns false the module stays unloaded and the failure is reported.

functions.name: sturdy_module_request_unload
functions.doc: Unloads a module: its `on_shutdown` runs, what it registered is removed, and it is destroyed. Refused when another module names it in `after`. Returns `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the game was not started with `sturdy_runtime_run_modules`.

functions.name: sturdy_module_take_failure
functions.doc: Takes the oldest message of a live change that failed, copying it out (see the string-output convention above); it is removed only when the copy succeeded, so a too-small buffer can be retried.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no change has failed since the last call drained them.

functions.name: sturdy_motion_blur_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (disabled — motion blur is opt-in).

functions.name: sturdy_native_available
functions.doc:
Reports whether raw native handles are available.

False when `SturdyRuntimeConfig::enable_native_access` was not set, or when the backend could not publish them. Check this before calling the getters below rather than treating their failure as fatal.

functions.name: sturdy_native_d3d12
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw D3D12 objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not D3D12, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_native_d3d12_queue
functions.doc: Reads the `ID3D12CommandQueue *` backing one queue lane.

params.name: queue_class
params.doc: Class of queue to resolve.

params.name: lane_index
params.doc: Lane within that class.

params.name: out_queue
params.doc: Receives the queue. Must not be null. Not `AddRef`'d.

functions.name: sturdy_native_vulkan
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw Vulkan objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not Vulkan, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_native_vulkan_queue
functions.doc: Reads the `VkQueue` and queue family index backing one queue lane.

params.name: queue_class
params.doc: Class of queue to resolve.

params.name: lane_index
params.doc: Lane within that class.

params.name: out_queue
params.doc: Receives the `VkQueue`. May be null.

params.name: out_queue_family_index
params.doc: Receives the Vulkan queue family index, which is what you need to create your own command pool against this queue. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_native_webgpu
functions.doc: Reads the engine's raw WebGPU objects.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the active backend is not WebGPU, or when native access was not enabled.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_language
functions.doc: The language the plugin reported through `set_info`, empty when it did not. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_load
functions.doc: Opens a plugin library and runs its entry point with `STURDY_PLUGIN_LOAD`, collecting its modules (nothing is started).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the library cannot be opened or exports no `sturdy_plugin_entry` (the cause is in the error message); `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` when the entry point refuses; the entry point's own error otherwise.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_module_count
functions.doc: How many modules the plugin added.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_module_name
functions.doc: The name of module `index`, in the order the plugin added them.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_name
functions.doc: The plugin's reported name (falls back to the file name).

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_release
functions.doc: Releases the caller's handle. The library closes once every module that was handed out has been destroyed (immediately when none was). Modules that were never handed out are destroyed now.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_load
functions.doc: Adds every module of the plugin to the running game (as `sturdy_module_request_load` for each, in the order added). Consumes the plugin's modules like `sturdy_plugin_take_modules`.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_reload
functions.doc: Replaces `previous`'s modules with `next`'s in the running game: same-named modules are reloaded in place, new ones are loaded, and names `previous` had that `next` lacks are unloaded. Consumes `next`'s modules. Release `previous` afterwards; its library closes when its modules are gone.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_request_unload
functions.doc: Unloads every module of `plugin` from the running game. Release the handle afterwards.

functions.name: sturdy_plugin_take_modules
functions.doc: Hands the plugin's modules to the caller, to pass to `sturdy_runtime_run_modules` (the returned strings and arrays stay valid until `sturdy_plugin_release`). Each module's ownership moves to whatever consumes it, so this works once per plugin: a second call returns `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY`. If `capacity` is smaller than the module count, `STURDY_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` is returned and nothing is handed out; `out_count` always receives the count.

functions.name: sturdy_presentation_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and the engine's defaults (vsync on, no HDR, opaque composition, automatic image count).

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_add_after_hook
functions.doc: Adds a listener that fires just after a method returns. See `sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook
functions.doc: Adds a listener that fires just before a method runs (with the same `args` the real call receives), in addition to — not instead of — the real implementation/override. Unlike `sturdy_reflection_register_override`, any number of mods may add hooks without clobbering each other's.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_clear_override
functions.doc: Removes a previously installed override, restoring the real implementation.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_get_element
functions.doc: Reads the element at `index` out of a container field.

params.name: element_size
params.doc: Must equal the container's declared element size.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `index >= sturdy_reflection_container_size(...)`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_resize
functions.doc: Resizes a container field to exactly `new_size` elements (default-constructing new ones, destroying truncated ones).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the element type has no default constructor.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_set_element
functions.doc: Writes `data` into the element at `index` of a container field. See `sturdy_reflection_container_get_element`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_container_size
functions.doc: Returns a container field's current element count.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_field_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a field.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_event
functions.doc: Looks up a declared hook point by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain. See `sturdy_reflection_find_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_field
functions.doc: Looks up a field by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain if not declared directly on it (the same behavior as `TypeRegistry::find_field`).
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no such field is declared on `type` or any ancestor.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_method
functions.doc: Looks up a method by name, walking `type`'s reflected base chain. See `sturdy_reflection_find_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_find_type
functions.doc: Looks up a reflected type by canonical name.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when nothing is registered under that name.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_fire_event
functions.doc: Fires an event, calling every subscribed listener in registration order. A no-op — cheap, no error — when nobody has subscribed.

params.name: args
params.doc: One already-typed pointer per event parameter. Pass null when the event takes none.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_get_field
functions.doc: Copies a field's current value out of `object` into `out_data`.

params.name: size
params.doc: Must equal the field's registered size (`SturdyReflectionFieldInfo::size`) — a mismatch is rejected rather than partially copied.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on a size mismatch or a field with no readable representation (an opaque non-`Trivial`, non-container field this ABI cannot copy).

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_get_static_field
functions.doc: Copies a static field's current value out. There is no per-instance object — the field has one true address, tracked internally.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_invoke_method
functions.doc: Calls an instance method on `object`, dispatching to a mod-installed override (`sturdy_reflection_register_override`) instead of the real implementation when one is present, and firing any before/after hooks around it either way.

params.name: args
params.doc: One already-typed pointer per parameter, in declared order (`SturdyReflectionMethodInfo::param_count` entries). Pass null when `param_count` is 0.

params.name: out_return
params.doc: Receives the return value (`out_return_size` bytes), ignored when the method returns nothing. May be null if you do not need it.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when `arg_count` does not match `param_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_invoke_static_method
functions.doc: Calls a static method. See `sturdy_reflection_invoke_method`; there is no receiver.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_method_info
functions.doc: Reads what the engine knows about a method.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_register_override
functions.doc: Installs a full replacement for a method — `sturdy_reflection_invoke_method`/ `_invoke_static_method` call `override_fn` instead of the real implementation from this point on. Only one override may be active per method; installing a second silently replaces the first (there is no chain — a mod that wants "wrap, not replace" should call through the before/after hooks instead, or capture and call the previous override itself before installing its own).

params.name: override_fn
params.doc: Must not be null. Pass a null-checking no-op and call `sturdy_reflection_clear_override` instead of passing null here to remove an override.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_remove_after_hook
functions.doc: Removes a hook added by `sturdy_reflection_add_after_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_remove_before_hook
functions.doc: Removes a hook added by `sturdy_reflection_add_before_hook`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_set_field
functions.doc: Overwrites a field's value in place on `object`. See `sturdy_reflection_get_field`.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on a size mismatch, a `ReadOnly` field, or a field with no writable representation.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_set_static_field
functions.doc: Overwrites a static field's value. See `sturdy_reflection_get_static_field`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_subscribe_event
functions.doc: Subscribes a listener to a declared hook point (`SFT_REFLECT_EVENT`). Any number of mods may subscribe to the same event independently.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_event
functions.doc: Declares one hook point on the type being built. See `SFT_REFLECT_EVENT`.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_field
functions.doc: Declares one field on the type being built.

params.name: is_trivial

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_add_method
functions.doc: Declares one method on the type being built.

params.name: param_types
params.doc: One id per parameter, in call order. May be null when `param_count` is 0.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_builder_create

params.name: align

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_type_size

functions.doc: Unregisters a type, so no future `find_type`/field/method/event lookup can reach it — the mod-unload primitive. See `TypeRegistry::unregister_type`'s C++ doc comment for the full quiescence requirement: stop dispatching to this type (no calls in flight against it on any thread) *before* calling this, and only unload any shared library it came from after.

functions.name: sturdy_reflection_unsubscribe_event

functions.name: sturdy_render_create_mesh_model
functions.doc: Creates a renderable model from your own geometry.

params.name: vertices
params.doc: Vertex array. Must not be null.

params.name: vertex_count
params.doc: Number of vertices.

params.name: indices
params.doc: Triangle indices, three per triangle. Every index must be less than `vertex_count`; this is checked, because an out-of-range index would otherwise read past the vertex buffer on the GPU.

params.name: index_count
params.doc: Number of indices. Must be a multiple of three.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader the model draws with.

params.name: label
params.doc: Debug label, or null.

params.doc: Receives the model asset.

params.name: shader
params.doc: Shader the model draws with.

params.name: out_model
params.doc: Receives the model asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_create_texture
functions.doc: Creates a texture asset directly from raw RGBA8 pixels — for a procedurally generated texture, as opposed to `sturdy_render_load_texture`/`sturdy_render_load_texture_from_memory`, which decode an encoded image format.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_shader
functions.doc:
Loads a shader from a Slang source file.

A model needs a shader, and the engine's standard one is `"Shaders/gbuffer_geometry.slang"` with a depth-only entry point of `"depthOnlyMain"` — that pairing is what the deferred renderer expects, so pass it unless you have written your own.

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to the shader source, relative to the working directory unless absolute.

params.name: depth_only_entry_point
params.doc: Depth-only fragment entry point, or null for none.

params.name: out_shader
params.doc: Receives the shader asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_texture
functions.doc: Loads a texture from an encoded image file (PNG, JPEG, and the rest the engine decodes).

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to the image file.

params.name: srgb
params.doc: Nonzero to treat the contents as sRGB, which is right for color maps and wrong for normal and roughness maps.

params.name: out_texture
params.doc: Receives the texture asset.

functions.name: sturdy_render_load_texture_from_memory
functions.doc: Decodes a texture from an in-memory encoded image (PNG, JPEG, and the rest the engine decodes) — the same decoder `sturdy_render_load_texture` uses, without requiring the bytes to already be a file on disk. For an image downloaded, generated, or packaged some other way.

params.name: encoded_bytes
params.doc: Encoded image bytes (a whole PNG/JPEG file's contents, not raw pixels).

params.name: encoded_size
params.doc: Length of `encoded_bytes`, in bytes. Must be nonzero.

params.name: srgb
params.doc: Nonzero to treat the contents as sRGB, which is right for color maps and wrong for normal and roughness maps.

params.name: out_texture
params.doc: Receives the texture asset.

functions.doc: Reports how much geometry a model asset holds.

params.name: out_primitives

params.name: out_vertices
params.doc: Receives the total vertex count. May be null.

params.name: out_triangles
params.doc: Receives the total triangle count. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_directional_light
functions.doc:
Makes an entity a directional light — the sun.

Direction comes from the entity's transform, so it needs one. Replaces any directional light the entity already has.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats. Values well above 1 are normal for a sun.

params.name: angular_radius_degrees
params.doc: Apparent size, which is what softens shadow edges. The real sun is about 0.27.

params.name: casts_shadows
params.doc: Nonzero to render shadow maps for this light.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_light_direction
functions.doc:
Reads back an entity's world transform.

Writes the entity's `WorldTransform` rotation, leaving no translation. Lights are the only renderable whose transform is read as a direction rather than a placement, and the axis it is taken from is an engine-internal convention, so this exists rather than asking a caller to construct the matrix. Use `sturdy_render_set_transform` when a light also needs a position.

params.name: engine
params.doc: Engine handle supplied to a game-logic callback.

params.name: entity
params.doc: Entity carrying a light component.

params.name: x
params.doc: Direction x component, in world space, pointing the way light travels.

params.name: y
params.doc: Direction y component.

params.name: z
params.doc: Direction z component.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK`; `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` when the direction is not finite or has zero length; a handle or entity error otherwise.
notes: This function does not throw exceptions.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model
functions.doc:
Makes an entity draw a model.

The entity also needs a transform to be drawn. Replaces any model the entity already has.

params.name: model
params.doc: Model asset to draw.

params.name: visible
params.doc: Nonzero to draw it. A hidden entity keeps its components and costs nothing to show again, which is cheaper than destroying and respawning it.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_float
functions.doc: Sets a scalar material parameter on one of a model's primitives.

params.name: primitive
params.doc: Which primitive to affect; 0 for a single-shape model.

params.name: name
params.doc: Parameter name as the shader declares it.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_texture
functions.doc: Binds a texture to a named slot on one of a model's primitives.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_model_vec4
functions.doc: Sets a four-component material parameter on one of a model's primitives.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_point_light
functions.doc: Makes an entity a point light. Position comes from its transform.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats.

params.name: range
params.doc: Distance beyond which the light contributes nothing.

params.name: source_radius
params.doc: Emitter radius, which softens shadows and highlights.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_spot_light
functions.doc: Makes an entity a spot light. Position and direction come from its transform.

params.name: radiance
params.doc: Linear RGB radiance, three floats.

params.name: range
params.doc: Distance beyond which the light contributes nothing.

params.name: inner_cone_degrees
params.doc: Half-angle of the fully lit cone.

params.name: outer_cone_degrees
params.doc: Half-angle at which the light has fallen off entirely. Must be at least `inner_cone_degrees`.

params.name: source_radius
params.doc: Emitter radius.

functions.name: sturdy_render_set_transform
functions.doc:
Gives an entity a world transform.

Rendering is driven from the ECS: an entity with a transform and a model is drawn, an entity with a transform and a light lights the scene. These helpers write the engine's own components rather than making you reproduce their memory layout — which you could do through `sturdy_ecs_add_component`, but only by hard-coding a layout that is free to change.

Replaces any transform the entity already has.

params.name: matrix
params.doc: Column-major 4x4 model matrix, 16 floats. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_shape_params_init
functions.doc: Fills `params` with the engine's default shape dimensions.

params.name: params
params.doc: Destination. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_render_spawn
functions.doc:
Creates an entity ready to be rendered, carrying an identity transform.

The natural way to start a renderable: an entity must be spawned with at least one component, and the engine's own components register themselves lazily the first time something uses them — so looking `sturdy.engine.world_transform` up by name before anything has touched it reports `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE`. This registers it and spawns in one step.

Follow with `sturdy_render_set_transform` to place it and `sturdy_render_set_model` or one of the light setters to give it something to contribute.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the new entity.

functions.name: sturdy_render_texture_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with engine defaults (linear color space, mipmaps and compression both on) and the correct `struct_size`. `width`, `height`, and `rgba8` are left for the caller to set.

functions.name: sturdy_render_unload_asset
functions.doc:
Unloads an asset — a model, shader, or texture previously created by `sturdy_render_load_shader`, `sturdy_render_create_shape_model`, `sturdy_render_create_mesh_model`, or `sturdy_render_load_texture`. This is the only way to release one; without it, every asset a long-running caller creates accumulates for the life of the engine.

Unloading does not check whether an entity's `sturdy_render_set_model` still points at it — despawn or reassign every such entity first, or its next draw reads a destroyed asset.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY` when `asset` is a shader or texture a loaded model still depends on; unload that model first. `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` when `asset` does not name a live asset.

functions.name: sturdy_restir_gi_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (Medium quality, SVGF denoiser, disabled — ReSTIR GI is opt-in).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_build_sizes
functions.doc: Queries the buffer sizes needed to build the acceleration structure described by `desc`. `desc->dst`/`src` are ignored; only `type`, `flags`, and `geometries` matter for sizing.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_acceleration_structure_device_address
functions.doc: Reads the GPU virtual address of `structure`, for writing into `SturdyAccelerationStructureInstance::acceleration_structure_device_address`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_adapter_info
functions.doc: Reads the active adapter's numeric identity.

params.name: out_info
params.doc: Destination. Must not be null; `struct_size` is written by the engine.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_adapter_string
functions.doc: Reads one of the adapter's text fields. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_backend
functions.doc:
Reports which graphics backend the engine actually created.

This is the resolved answer, never `STURDY_BACKEND_DEFAULT`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_buffer_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (`STURDY_MEMORY_LOCATION_DEVICE_LOCAL`, no usage flags, zero size).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_buffer_device_address
functions.doc: Reads the GPU virtual address of `buffer`. Requires the buffer to have been created with storage/indirect/acceleration-structure-input usage that publishes a device address on the active backend.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_barrier
functions.doc: Inserts a pipeline barrier. Any of the three arrays may be empty (count 0, pointer null).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_compute_pass
functions.doc: Begins a compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_pipeline_statistics_query
functions.doc: Begins a pipeline-statistics query at `query_set[index]`, ended by `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_end_pipeline_statistics_query`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_PIPELINE_STATISTICS` query set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_begin_render_pass
functions.doc: Begins a render pass. `desc->color_attachments` is read synchronously and need not outlive the call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_build_acceleration_structures
functions.doc: Builds or updates `build_count` acceleration structures, recorded into the command encoder outside any render/compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_build_opacity_micromaps
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_color_texture
functions.doc: Clears a color texture's subresources to a solid color, outside any render pass.
notes: `texture` must have been created with `STURDY_TEXTURE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT`. Vulkan's `vkCmdClearColorImage` has no such requirement, but D3D12 clears through a render-target view, so this is required for portability across both backends even though only one enforces it — verified empirically against both.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_depth_stencil_texture
functions.doc: Clears a depth/stencil texture's subresources, outside any render pass.
notes: `texture` should be created with `STURDY_TEXTURE_USAGE_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT`; by symmetry with `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_clear_color_texture` above, D3D12 likely clears through a depth-stencil view the same way, though this has not been independently verified against both backends the way the color case was.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_buffer_to_buffer
functions.doc: Copies bytes between two buffers.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_buffer_to_texture
functions.doc: Copies bytes from a buffer into a texture's subresources.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_texture_to_buffer
functions.doc: Copies texels from a texture's subresources into a buffer.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_copy_texture_to_texture
functions.doc: Copies texels between two textures' subresources.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (graphics queue, lane 0).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_end_pipeline_statistics_query
functions.doc: Ends the most recently begun pipeline-statistics query on this encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_fill_buffer
functions.doc: Fills a byte range of `buffer` with repeated copies of `value`, outside any render/compute pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_finish
functions.doc: Ends recording and produces a submittable command buffer. `encoder` is consumed: its token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_pop_debug_group
functions.doc: Pops the most recently pushed debug group.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_push_debug_group
functions.doc: Pushes a labeled debug group, for graphics-debugger capture readability.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_release
functions.doc: Abandons an in-progress recording without submitting it. Use `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_finish` instead when the recorded commands should actually run.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_reset_query_set
functions.doc: Resets `count` queries starting at `first` to the unavailable state, recorded into the command encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_resolve_query_set
functions.doc: Copies `count` query results starting at `first` from `query_set` into `dst` at `dst_offset`, entirely on the GPU. Prefer this over `sturdy_rhi_get_query_set_results` when the results feed a later GPU pass rather than the host (e.g. GPU-driven culling statistics).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_set_ray_tracing_pipeline
functions.doc: Binds the ray tracing pipeline used by a subsequent `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_trace_rays`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_trace_rays
functions.doc: Dispatches rays against the pipeline bound by `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_set_ray_tracing_pipeline`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_update_buffer
functions.doc: Records a GPU-timed write of `data` into `buffer` at `offset`, outside any render/compute pass. Prefer this over `sturdy_rhi_write_buffer` for a write that must be ordered against other commands in the same encoder.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_write_timestamp
functions.doc: Writes a GPU timestamp for `query_set[index]` once every command before this point in the encoder has reached `stage`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP` query set.

params.name: stage
params.doc: A single `STURDY_PIPELINE_STAGE_*` value (not a combination) naming the point in the pipeline to timestamp.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_compute_pass_dispatch_indirect
functions.doc: Dispatches using group counts read from `indirect_buffer` at `offset` (three consecutive `uint32_t`s), written by an earlier pass on the GPU.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_compute_pass_end
functions.doc: Ends the compute pass. `pass`'s token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails. The parent command encoder may be used again afterward.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group_layout

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_buffer

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_command_encoder
functions.doc: Begins recording a new command buffer.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_compute_pipeline

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_opacity_micromap
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_pipeline_layout

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_query_set

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_create_render_bundle_encoder
functions.doc: Begins recording a render bundle.

functions.doc: Destroys a bind group created by `sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_bind_group_layout
functions.doc: Destroys a bind group layout created by `sturdy_rhi_create_bind_group_layout`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.doc: Destroys a buffer created by `sturdy_rhi_create_buffer`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.doc: Destroys a semaphore created by `sturdy_rhi_create_semaphore`. A null/zero handle is a no-op.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_destroy_shader_module

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_device_limits
functions.doc: Reads the active device's hardware limits.

functions.doc: Reads the enabled extension at `index` as `"<namespace>.<name>"`, with its version.

params.name: out_version
params.doc: Receives the extension version. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_count
functions.doc:
Returns how many RHI features exist in this engine build.

Features are addressed by index rather than by a mirrored C enum on purpose: the engine defines several hundred of them and adds more over time, and restating that list here would guarantee the two drift apart. Enumerate names with `sturdy_rhi_feature_name`, or resolve a known name to its index once at startup with `sturdy_rhi_feature_index`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_enabled
functions.doc: Reports whether the feature at `index` was actually enabled on the active device.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_index
functions.doc: Resolves a feature name to its index.

params.name: name
params.doc: Null-terminated feature name, matching `sturdy_rhi_feature_name` exactly.

params.name: out_index
params.doc: Receives the index.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when this build has no feature by that name — which is also how a binding detects that it is running against an older engine.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_feature_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of the feature at `index`. See the string-output convention above.

params.name: index
params.doc: Feature index, less than `sturdy_rhi_feature_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_get_query_set_results
functions.doc: Reads back `count` results starting at `first`, into `dst` (which must be at least `count * stride` bytes). Blocks the host if `STURDY_QUERY_RESULT_FLAGS_WAIT` is set; otherwise a query whose result is not yet available reads as undefined unless `STURDY_QUERY_RESULT_FLAGS_PARTIAL` is also set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_map_buffer
functions.doc: Maps `buffer` for host access. Only valid for a buffer created with a host-visible `SturdyMemoryLocation`.

params.name: out_ptr
params.doc: Receives a pointer to the mapped range, valid until `sturdy_rhi_unmap_buffer`.

params.name: out_size
params.doc: Receives the mapped range's size in bytes. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_opacity_micromap_build_sizes
