functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and zeroed contents (no color formats, no depth/stencil format, `samples = 1`) — set `color_formats` before use.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect
functions.doc: D3D12 does not allow indirect draws of any kind — including mesh-tasks-indirect — inside a bundle; this reports a backend failure there rather than an ABI-level rejection, matching how the ordinary indirect-draw bundle restriction behaves.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect_count
functions.doc: See `sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect`'s D3D12 caveat.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_finish
functions.doc: Finishes recording, consuming `encoder` (its token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails) and producing a replayable `SturdyRenderBundle`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_encoder_release
functions.doc: Abandons an in-progress bundle recording without finishing it. `encoder`'s token is invalid after this call.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_bundle_set_bind_group
functions.doc: Binds a bind group at `index`. Same `dynamic_offsets` convention as `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_bind_group`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_begin_occlusion_query
functions.doc: Begins an occlusion query at `query_set[index]`, ended by `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end_occlusion_query`. Only valid for a `STURDY_QUERY_TYPE_OCCLUSION` query set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and zeroed contents (no color attachments, no depth/stencil attachment, zero render area — set `color_attachments`/`render_area` before use).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect_count
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indexed_indirect_multi
functions.doc: Indexed counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_multi`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect
functions.doc: Draws using arguments read from `indirect_buffer` at `offset` (a single `SturdyDrawArgs`-shaped record, engine-native layout matching the active backend's indirect-draw structure).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count
functions.doc: Issues up to `max_draws` draws read from `indirect_buffer`, with the actual count read from a 32-bit value in `count_buffer` at `count_offset` (clamped to `max_draws`). Backed by `vkCmdDrawIndirectCount` on Vulkan and `ExecuteIndirect` with a counter resource on D3D12.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_multi
functions.doc: Issues `draw_count` draws read from consecutive `stride`-byte records in `indirect_buffer` starting at `offset`. `draw_count` is fixed at record time; use `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count` when the count itself comes from the GPU.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks
functions.doc: Dispatches the mesh (and, if present, task) shader stages of the currently bound pipeline, which must have been created with `SturdyRenderPipelineDesc::mesh` set. Neither backend clamps `group_count_*` against a device maximum here — an out-of-range value is a backend- defined failure, the same as a C++ caller would see.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect
functions.doc: Mesh-shader counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect`: dispatch dimensions are read from a single `SturdyDrawMeshTasksArgs`-shaped record in `indirect_buffer` at `offset`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_mesh_tasks_indirect_count
functions.doc: Mesh-shader counterpart to `sturdy_rhi_render_pass_draw_indirect_count`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end
functions.doc: Ends the render pass. `pass`'s token is invalid after this call, whether it succeeds or fails. The parent command encoder may be used again afterward.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_end_occlusion_query
functions.doc: Ends the most recently begun occlusion query on this render pass.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_execute_bundles
functions.doc: Replays `bundles` into `pass`, which must have been created with `SturdyRenderPassDesc::allow_bundles` set.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_bind_group
functions.doc: Binds a bind group at `index`. `dynamic_offsets` supplies one offset per dynamic-offset binding in the group's layout, in declaration order; pass null/0 when the layout has none.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_blend_constant
functions.doc: Sets the constant blend color used by `STURDY_BLEND_FACTOR_CONSTANT_COLOR`/ `STURDY_BLEND_FACTOR_ONE_MINUS_CONSTANT_COLOR`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_index_buffer
functions.doc: Binds the index buffer used by subsequent indexed draws.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_pipeline
functions.doc: Sets the pipeline used by subsequent draws.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_push_constants
functions.doc: Writes push-constant bytes visible to `stages`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pass_set_vertex_buffer
functions.doc: Binds a vertex buffer at `slot`, matching the pipeline's `vertex_buffers` layout array index.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_render_pipeline_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (triangle list, fill/back-cull/CCW rasterization, no multisampling, no depth/stencil, no color targets, zeroed shader entries).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_reset_fences
functions.doc: Resets one or more fences to unsignaled.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_reset_query_set
functions.doc: Resets `count` queries starting at `first` to the unavailable state, outside any command encoder. Every query must be reset (via this or `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_reset_query_set`) before its first use.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_sampler_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (linear filtering/mipmapping, repeat addressing, LOD range [0, 1000], no anisotropy, no comparison).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_semaphore_value
functions.doc: Reads the semaphore's current counter value.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_signal_semaphore
functions.doc: Advances `semaphore`'s counter to `value` from the host. Rarely needed directly — a submission with a signal entry (see `sturdy_rhi_submit`) is the usual way a semaphore advances.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_submit
functions.doc: Submits finished command buffers to a device queue for execution.

params.name: fence
params.doc: Optional; the zero handle submits with no fence. When supplied, it becomes signaled once this submission's work completes — wait on it with `sturdy_rhi_wait_fences` rather than `sturdy_rhi_wait_idle` to know when it is safe to reuse or destroy the submitted command buffers. This is the one-shot GPU-work pattern: create a fence, submit with it, wait on it, destroy the fence and command buffer.

params.name: one_shot
params.doc: Hints that these command buffers will not be resubmitted, letting the backend release their recording resources as soon as this submission completes.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_texture_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills `desc` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (2D, `STURDY_FORMAT_UNDEFINED`, 1x1x1, one mip level, one sample, no usage flags).

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_unmap_buffer
functions.doc: Unmaps a buffer previously mapped with `sturdy_rhi_map_buffer`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_wait_fences
functions.doc: Waits for one or more fences to become signaled — the correct way to know a specific submission has finished. Prefer this over `sturdy_rhi_wait_idle`, which is a device-wide barrier and unsafe to interleave with any other GPU work in flight, including the engine's own.

params.name: wait_all
params.doc: `STURDY_TRUE` to wait for every fence; `STURDY_FALSE` to return once any one is signaled.

params.name: timeout_ns
params.doc: Maximum time to wait, in nanoseconds. `STURDY_WAIT_FOREVER` for no timeout.

params.name: out_signaled
params.doc: Receives whether the wait condition was met (`STURDY_FALSE` on timeout). May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_wait_idle
functions.doc: Blocks until every queue on the active device has finished all submitted work. Expensive, and unsafe to call while any other GPU work — including the engine's own internal one-shot uploads — may still be in flight on this device. Intended for shutdown/resource-teardown synchronization; wait on a specific submission with `sturdy_rhi_wait_fences` instead.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_wait_semaphore
functions.doc: Blocks the calling host thread until `semaphore`'s counter reaches `value`.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_write_buffer
functions.doc: Uploads `data` into `buffer` at `offset`, outside any command encoder. Suitable for infrequent, host-visible writes; for per-frame or GPU-timed writes use `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_update_buffer` instead.

functions.name: sturdy_rhi_write_ray_tracing_shader_group_handles
functions.doc: Reads `group_count` shader group handles starting at `first_group`, into `dst` (which must be at least `group_count * sturdy_rhi_ray_tracing_properties`'s `shader_group_handle_size` bytes). Write these into a shader binding table buffer at `shader_group_base_alignment`-aligned offsets to build `SturdyShaderBindingTableRegion`s for `sturdy_rhi_command_encoder_trace_rays`.

functions.name: sturdy_runtime_config_init
functions.doc:
Fills `config` with engine defaults and the correct `struct_size`.

Always call this before setting fields. It is what makes a binding compiled against an older header keep working against a newer engine: fields you have never heard of still get sane values instead of whatever was on your stack.

params.name: config
params.doc: Destination. Must not be null.

functions.name: sturdy_runtime_run
functions.doc:
Runs the application to completion: creates the window and graphics device, drives the frame loop, and returns once the last window closes.

Blocks the calling thread for the entire lifetime of the application. Only one runtime may be active per process; a concurrent or nested call fails with `STURDY_ERROR_ALREADY_RUNNING` rather than corrupting the first one's state.

params.name: config
params.doc: Configuration, previously initialized by `sturdy_runtime_config_init`.

params.name: game_logic
params.doc: Your callbacks. Must not be null, though its individual callbacks may be. `destroy` is invoked before this function returns, on every path including failure.

params.name: argc
params.doc: Number of command-line arguments in `argv`. Pass 0 with a null `argv` if you have none; the engine parses its own recognized flags from these.

params.name: argv
params.doc: Command-line arguments as null-terminated UTF-8. May be null only when `argc` is 0.

params.name: out_exit_code
params.doc: Receives the application's own exit code. Written whenever the runtime actually ran, including when this function goes on to return `STURDY_ERROR_CALLBACK_FAILED`. May be null.

functions.returns: `STURDY_OK` when the runtime ran to completion — check `out_exit_code` for the application's own status, which is nonzero if it terminated unhappily. `STURDY_ERROR_CALLBACK_FAILED` when one of your callbacks reported failure, and `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` when the engine never came up at all (no window, no graphics device, or a `physical_device_id` this machine does not have). Those three are kept distinct so a binding can tell its own rejection apart from an engine failure apart from an ordinary nonzero exit. Argument and configuration problems are reported before anything starts.

functions.name: sturdy_runtime_run_modules
functions.doc:
Like `sturdy_runtime_run`, for a game made of several modules (since 0.35).

Modules start in the order you list them, adjusted so each comes after the modules in its `after` list; they shut down in the reverse order. If a module's `on_engine_initialized` returns false (or a dependency is unknown or cyclic), every module that had started is shut down and the call returns `STURDY_ERROR_CALLBACK_FAILED` (or `STURDY_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` for a bad dependency, with the cause in the engine log).

For each frame every module's `request_render_frame` runs in start order. Among modules with `contributes_scene`, the last one that returns true supplies the camera, lighting and render graph; every module's overlay passes are kept, in start order. If no scene module returns true the frame is skipped.

Threading is as for `sturdy_runtime_run`: `request_render_frame` may run on per-window render threads, so a module's own state must be safe for that. The module list never changes after startup.

params.name: modules
params.doc: `module_count` modules. Checked before anything starts: a bad struct size, an empty or duplicate name, a module that lists itself in `after`, or no modules at all returns `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (or `STURDY_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_STRUCT_SIZE`) and no `destroy` hook is run, so you still own every `user_data`. Once the runtime starts, each module's `destroy` is invoked exactly once on every path.

functions.name: sturdy_scene_clip_count
functions.doc: Returns how many animation clips the imported scene carries.

functions.name: sturdy_scene_clip_duration
functions.doc: Reads the length of clip `index` in seconds.

functions.name: sturdy_scene_clip_name
functions.doc: Reads the name of clip `index`. See the string-output convention above.

functions.name: sturdy_scene_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (raster deferred, path tracing parameters set but unused until `integrator` selects a path-traced mode).

functions.name: sturdy_scene_spawn
functions.doc: Spawns every model and light of the scene with its animation wired up: skinned characters get a private deformable copy and an animator, blend-shape meshes likewise, and plain animated nodes follow the file's node animation. `sturdy_gltf_spawn_all` is this with default options.

params.name: options
params.doc: Null for the defaults.

params.name: out_entities
params.doc: Optional array receiving the created entities (renderers first, then lights).

params.name: capacity
params.doc: Length of `out_entities`.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many entities were created (may exceed `capacity`). May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_screen_space_gi_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (disabled).

functions.name: sturdy_shadow_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (4 cascades, 4096 atlas, contact shadows on, contact hardening off).

functions.name: sturdy_sound_load
functions.doc: Decodes a file (any supported codec; cached by path) without playing it.

functions.name: sturdy_sound_play
functions.doc: Plays a loaded sound. `out_voice` may be null for fire-and-forget; a returned voice must still be released.

functions.name: sturdy_spawn_options_init
functions.doc: Fills `options` with the defaults: auto-play, looping, speed 1, first clip, identity transform.

functions.name: sturdy_surface_presentation_resolution
functions.doc: Reads what `surface`'s presentation policy actually resolved to.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when `surface` has not rendered a frame yet (no swapchain exists to report on).

functions.name: sturdy_surface_presentation_settings
functions.doc: Reads `surface`'s current presentation policy: the last value `sturdy_surface_set_presentation_settings` accepted, or the app-wide default if never overridden.

functions.name: sturdy_surface_query_hdr_capabilities
functions.doc: Queries `surface`'s real HDR display capabilities and supported presentation modes.

params.name: out_capabilities
params.doc: Receives the capability summary. Must not be null.

params.name: out_modes
params.doc: Receives up to `modes_capacity` supported transfer-function/gamut combinations. May be null if `modes_capacity` is 0.

params.name: out_mode_count
params.doc: Receives the number of modes the display actually supports, which may exceed `modes_capacity`. May be null.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when `surface` has not rendered a frame yet (no RHI surface exists to query). A supported-but-empty answer is not an ABI error — see `SturdyHdrCapabilities::status` for that.

functions.name: sturdy_surface_set_presentation_settings
functions.doc: Requests a change to `surface`'s presentation policy. Queued like a window request: applied the next time `surface` renders, not synchronously.

functions.name: sturdy_surface_update_hdr_content_light_level
functions.doc: Updates HDR10 static content light level metadata (MaxCLL/MaxFALL) on `surface`'s live swapchain, without recreating it.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when `surface` has no live swapchain yet, or when the active backend/driver cannot update this metadata live (e.g. Vulkan without `VK_EXT_hdr_metadata`).

functions.name: sturdy_time_delta_seconds
functions.doc:
Reads the time step for the current tick, after the time scale is applied.

This is the value gameplay should integrate against. It differs from `SturdyFrameInput`'s `delta_seconds`, which is raw per-surface frame time and ignores the scale entirely.

functions.name: sturdy_time_scale
functions.doc: Reads the current time scale. 1.0 is real time, 0.0 is fully paused.

functions.name: sturdy_time_set_scale
functions.doc: Sets the time scale.

params.name: scale
params.doc: Multiplier applied to the simulation step. Must be finite and non-negative; negative values are rejected rather than running the simulation backwards, which nothing downstream is written to handle.

functions.name: sturdy_time_tick_index
functions.doc: Reads the monotonically increasing simulation tick counter.

functions.name: sturdy_time_unscaled_delta_seconds
functions.doc:
Reads the time step for the current tick before the time scale is applied.

Use this for anything that must keep running at real speed while the game is slowed or paused — UI animation, profiling, input smoothing.

functions.name: sturdy_tone_mapping_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (AGX operator, no look, neutral PsychoV/Hermite curve parameters).

functions.name: sturdy_trace_capture
functions.doc: Replaces the calling thread's trace with the stack at this call (foreign site, engine scopes, native stack per the detail setting). For a foreign language that wants the engine's side of a stack at a moment of its choosing, such as a panic hook.

functions.name: sturdy_trace_clear_foreign_call_site
functions.doc: Forgets the calling thread's foreign call site.

functions.name: sturdy_trace_get_detail
functions.doc: Reads the current capture detail.

functions.name: sturdy_trace_install_crash_handler
functions.doc: Installs process-wide crash handlers (fatal signals on POSIX, the unhandled-exception filter on Windows) that print the crashing thread's engine scopes and native stack before the process dies. Does nothing useful on WebAssembly (returns `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE`). Safe to call repeatedly.

params.name: log_path
params.doc: Also append the report to this file; null or empty for stderr only.

functions.name: sturdy_trace_set_detail
functions.doc: Chooses how much future failures capture, for the whole process.

functions.name: sturdy_trace_set_foreign_call_site
functions.doc: Announces where the calling thread's foreign code is, so a failure inside the engine can be traced back to a line of it. The site stays in force until replaced or cleared, so announcing once per frame or per widget is as valid as before every call. The engine copies the strings (they need not be null-terminated or outlive the call), and re-announcing an identical site allocates nothing.

params.name: language
params.doc: Short tag: "rust", "csharp", "java", "python", ...

params.name: file
params.doc: Source file; may be empty.

params.name: line
params.doc: 1-based line, or 0 if unknown.

params.name: column
params.doc: 1-based column, or 0 if unknown.

params.name: function
params.doc: Enclosing function; may be empty.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_begin
functions.doc:
Opens a UI frame, to be built and then closed with `sturdy_ui_end`.

Call this from `request_render_frame` before building any UI. It readies the UI renderer, starts a layout pass sized to the surface, and picks up this frame's pointer state so hover and click queries work.

Between begin and end, the ABI holds an open layout. Build the tree, then call `sturdy_ui_end` on every path — including when you decide not to render the frame — or the next frame's begin reports `STURDY_ERROR_BUSY`.

params.name: input
params.doc: This frame's input, as handed to `request_render_frame`.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` if the UI renderer could not be created, which is not fatal — skip UI for this frame and try again next.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_begin_element
functions.doc: Opens an element. Children declared until the matching `sturdy_ui_end_element` go inside it.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_clicked
functions.doc: Reports whether the element with this id was clicked this frame.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_element_init
functions.doc: Fills an element declaration with defaults: fit sizing, no padding, transparent, left-to-right.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_end
functions.doc:
Closes the UI frame and attaches the result to `frame` as an overlay.

Every element opened with `sturdy_ui_begin_element` must be closed first.

params.name: frame
params.doc: The frame being configured, as handed to `request_render_frame`. Pass a zeroed handle to discard the UI instead of drawing it.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_end_element
functions.doc:
Closes the most recently opened element.

Reports `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` if nothing is open, rather than unbalancing the tree.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_axis_init
functions.doc: Fills an axis config with defaults: linear scale, autoscaled, 6 target ticks, gridlines on.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_desc_init
functions.doc: Fills a graph description with defaults: a Line chart with linear, autoscaled axes and the engine's default colors/margins.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_draw
functions.doc: Draws a graph/plot widget as a leaf element inside the current UI frame, sized/positioned by `element` the same way `sturdy_ui_begin_element`'s element is. See the engine-side `SFT::UI::graph()`'s own doc comment for the bounds-latency contract (one frame behind a layout change, same as every other bounds-dependent widget).

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_series_clear
functions.doc: Removes every sample from `series`, without releasing it.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_series_create
functions.doc: Creates an owned, incrementally-appendable data series — the ring-buffer convenience for live/ streaming telemetry.

params.name: capacity
params.doc: Bounds how many trailing `(x, y)` samples are kept; once full, the oldest sample is dropped as a new one is pushed (a "tail -f" window). `0` means unbounded.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_series_data
functions.doc: Reads back `series`' current samples as flat arrays, to bind into a `SturdyUiGraphSeriesRef`'s `x_data`/`y_data`.
functions.returns: `out_x`/`out_y` are borrowed and valid only until the next call that mutates this series (push/clear/release) on this thread — use them immediately, in the same `sturdy_ui_graph_draw` call.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_series_push
functions.doc: Appends one `(x, y)` sample to `series`.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_graph_series_release
functions.doc: Releases a data series created with `sturdy_ui_graph_series_create`. Unknown/already-released tokens are ignored.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_hovered
functions.doc:
Reports whether the pointer is over the element with this id.

Reflects the previous frame's layout, which is how immediate-mode UI works: an element's bounds are not known until it has been laid out once.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_pointer_down
functions.doc: Reports whether the pointer is currently held down.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_pointer_position
functions.doc: Reads the pointer position in UI coordinates: the same units as element sizes and positions, which are framebuffer pixels divided by the content scale unless `STURDY_UI_SCALE_MODE_RAW_PIXELS` is set.

params.name: out_x
params.doc: Receives the horizontal position. May be null.

params.name: out_y
params.doc: Receives the vertical position. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_register_font
functions.doc:
Loads a font file and registers it under `font_id`.

Text draws nothing until a font is registered, so do this once during `on_engine_initialized`. `font_id` 0 is the default the text style starts with.

params.name: source
params.doc: Path to a TTF or OTF file.

params.name: font_id
params.doc: Identifier to register it under.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_set_scale_mode
functions.doc: Chooses how UI units map onto the framebuffer. Takes effect at the next `sturdy_ui_begin`.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an unknown mode.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_text
functions.doc: Draws text inside the current element.

params.name: text
params.doc: Null-terminated UTF-8.

functions.name: sturdy_ui_text_style_init
functions.doc: Fills a text style with defaults: font 0, 16px, opaque white.

functions.name: sturdy_voice_set_position
functions.doc: Moves a spatial voice; `velocity` (may be null) feeds Doppler shift.

functions.name: sturdy_volumetric_fog_settings_init
functions.doc: Fills `settings` with `struct_size` and engine defaults (disabled — fog is opt-in).

functions.name: sturdy_window_config_init
functions.doc: Fills `config` with the engine's default window configuration (1280x720, windowed, decorated, visible, resizable, OS-placed).

functions.name: sturdy_window_content_scale
functions.doc: Reads the UI scale the OS asks for on the display the window is on (1.0 at 100%, 2.0 at 200%). Updated when the window moves to a display with a different scale.

params.name: surface
params.doc: Surface identifier, as handed to `request_render_frame`.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no managed window matches.

functions.name: sturdy_window_count
functions.doc: Returns how many windows the engine currently manages.

functions.name: sturdy_window_find
functions.doc: Reads the window a surface belongs to.

params.name: surface
params.doc: Surface identifier, as handed to `request_render_frame`.

functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when no managed window matches.

functions.name: sturdy_window_primary
functions.doc: Reads the primary window.
functions.returns: `STURDY_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE` when there is no primary window, which is the case during teardown after it has closed.

functions.name: sturdy_window_recreate_primary
functions.doc:
Requests that the primary window be destroyed and recreated with a new configuration — changing decorations or transparency after creation on a platform where the window must be recreated to do so, for instance.

Queued and completion-reported the same way as `sturdy_window_spawn`.

params.name: out_request_id
params.doc: Receives an identifier for the queued request. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_window_request_close
functions.doc:
Requests that a window close.

Queued rather than immediate: the engine applies window changes at a defined point in the frame so a request made from a render callback cannot destroy the window being drawn. Every function in this section behaves that way.

params.name: out_request_id
params.doc: Receives an identifier for the queued request. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_cursor_grabbed
functions.doc: Requests that a window grab (confine) or release the cursor at the OS level.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_cursor_icon
functions.doc: Requests a cursor shape for a window.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_decorated
functions.doc: Requests that a window show or hide its system decorations.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_effect
functions.doc:
Requests a platform-composited visual effect for a window (Windows' Mica/Acrylic/blur, etc.).

Queued like every other request in this section: this call only reports a bad engine handle or argument. Whether the platform actually supports `kind` is decided when the request is applied, and (like every other queued window request) that outcome is not currently reported back.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_mode
functions.doc: Requests a windowed/fullscreen mode change.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_mouse_locked
functions.doc: Requests that a window confine the cursor to its bounds while keeping it visible at an absolute position — see `SturdyWindowSnapshot::mouse_locked` for the resulting state. Distinct from `sturdy_window_set_relative_mouse_mode`, which also hides the cursor and switches to unbounded motion deltas.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_relative_mouse_mode
functions.doc: Requests relative mouse mode (the OS cursor is hidden and confined, and mouse motion reports as unbounded deltas instead of absolute position) for a window — the mode a first-person camera or any other mouse-look control needs. See `SturdyWindowSnapshot::mouse_locked` and `sturdy_engine_mouse_delta` for reading the resulting state and motion.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_text_input_active
functions.doc: Requests that a window start or stop IME text composition (on-screen keyboards, CJK input methods, etc.). Most text fields need this active only while focused and editable.

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_text_input_area
functions.doc: Hints the IME where to draw its candidate/composition window, in window coordinates. Only meaningful while text input is active (see `sturdy_window_set_text_input_active`).

functions.name: sturdy_window_set_transparent
functions.doc: Requests that a window become transparent or opaque.

functions.name: sturdy_window_snapshot
functions.doc: Reads the window at `index`.

functions.name: sturdy_window_spawn
functions.doc:
Requests a new, additional window.

Queued like every other request in this section: this only reports a bad engine handle, argument, or struct-size mismatch. Whether the window was actually created is reported later through `sturdy_window_take_completions`, keyed by `*out_request_id`.

params.name: out_request_id
params.doc: Receives an identifier for the queued request. May be null.

functions.name: sturdy_window_take_completions
functions.doc: Copies up to `capacity` completed window requests into `out_completions` and reports the true number available in `*out_count`, which may exceed `capacity` — completions beyond `capacity` are dropped, not held for a later call, since window lifecycle events are rare enough that a caller should simply pass a generously sized buffer (8 is enough for any realistic frame).

params.name: out_completions
params.doc: May be null only when `capacity` is 0, to just read `*out_count`.
